text: When adding or modifying templates/components, provide a corresponding pattern-library preview: a dedicated template under `styleguide/` (named after the component) and a paired `.yaml` context fixture. The fixture must supply representative, hard-coded sample data (never live DB queries) and define exactly the variables the template consumes; remove any stale keys. Mark temporary mocks/placeholders with a comment explaining what will replace them.
reason: Pattern library previews must render independently of database state, remain deterministic, and stay in sync with their templates to serve as reliable, isolated examples for design/QA review.
common_pattern: Pattern library maintenance for templates: ensuring each new or modified template/component has a proper isolated preview with representative, non‑DB mock data and stays in sync with its fixture.

text: When renaming or replacing a StreamField block type, update every matching block definition across the shared blocks module (including occurrences nested inside other blocks) and account for persisted data via a StreamField data migration or manual re-adding of affected content, since stored StreamField JSON references the old block type name.
reason: Incomplete refactors leave mixed usage of old and new block types and inconsistent behavior, while renaming without a migration breaks or loses existing persisted content.
scope: module/file, and codebase-wide for repeated block types
common_pattern: StreamField block type lifecycle management: how blocks should be named by content, and what must be done across the codebase (occurrences + persisted data) when a block type is renamed or replaced.

text: Within each import section, keep third-party imports alphabetically sorted regardless of whether the statement uses `import x` or `from x import y`. Enforce this by configuring the project's import sorter (e.g. ruff/isort `force-sort-within-sections`) instead of manually reordering generated files such as Django migrations.
reason: Alphabetical import ordering makes dependencies easier to scan and avoids large, noisy diffs caused by default isort behavior grouping straight imports before from imports. Adjusting shared linter configuration addresses the source of churn across regenerated files.
common_pattern: Import ordering: keep third-party imports alphabetically sorted within their section, and enforce this via shared linter configuration rather than manual reordering, especially for generated files.

text: Import every referenced model or class from its canonical module; local `.models` imports only provide project-specific classes, so Wagtail built-in models must be imported explicitly from their `wagtail.*.models` path (e.g., `from wagtail.images.models import Image`).
reason: Prevents `NameError` and keeps dependencies explicit when local project models and framework built-in models coexist.
common_pattern: Explicit imports for non-local models: when code references a model/class not defined locally (particularly Wagtail built-in models alongside local project models), import it from its canonical module path rather than relying on implicit or local re-exports.

text: In Django/Wagtail templates, ensure every `{% load %}` declaration is accurate: load a custom template tag library before using its tags or filters, and remove `{% load %}` libraries that are no longer referenced in that template.
reason: Accurate load declarations prevent rendering errors from missing libraries while avoiding unused imports that add noise and imply false dependencies.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns govern correct organization and use of Django/Wagtail custom template tag libraries: `{% load %}` declarations should match actual usage, and app-specific tag libraries should live in the owning app's `templatetags/` directory.

text: Before adding OS packages via `apt-get install` in a Dockerfile, verify the package name and version exist in the base image's configured repositories; if a specific version is required, add the upstream repository explicitly instead of assuming availability.
reason: Prevents build failures such as `E: Unable to locate package <name>` caused by packages unavailable for the base distribution.
common_pattern: Docker/container image and dependency version pinning must be consistent and intentional — pin to an explicit, currently-supported release; align local compose images with deployed environments; and keep version references (tags, ARGs, comments) synchronized. The cluster mixes several distinct-but-related version-hygiene sub-patterns rather than one single principle.

text: Declare the compiler/language package explicitly in `devDependencies` when the build tooling or lint/format scripts target that language (e.g. add `typescript` when using `ts-loader` with `.ts`/`.tsx` globs). Do not rely on it being pulled in transitively through a loader or plugin.
reason: Transitive dependencies of loaders/plugins are not guaranteed to remain available or version-compatible; the compiler must be a direct, pinned dependency for reproducible builds and type-checking.
common_pattern: When tooling indicates a compiler or language is part of the build/lint/format pipeline, that compiler/language package must be declared as an explicit devDependency instead of relied on transitively.

text: In Wagtail projects, avoid bundling or injecting raw font assets. Use Wagtail's system font and maintained icon integrations such as `wagtail-font-awesome-svg` instead, and remove now-unnecessary webpack font loaders and dependencies.
reason: Reduces unused webpack configuration and unnecessary dependencies, and aligns font/icon asset handling with Wagtail's system-supported and maintained approaches.
common_pattern: In Wagtail projects, prefer Wagtail's built-in/system-supported asset handling and maintained integrations over bundling or injecting raw font assets and their associated loaders/dependencies.

text: Do not add global font-weight variables for a single page type; when additional weights are only needed on specific pages, load them as separate font files scoped to those pages instead of adding them to the global/site-wide font set.
reason: Global font weights are bundled for every page, so adding weights used by only one page type bloats the font payload site-wide (e.g. 40KB → 160KB). Scoping extra fonts avoids shipping unused weights to all pages.
common_pattern: Web font payload/performance management: limiting which font weights ship site-wide and shipping them in an efficient production format. Both generalizations target reducing font asset weight/size for page performance.

text: Serve web font assets (including variable fonts) in `woff2` format for production rather than `.ttf` or `truetype-variations`.
reason: `woff2` provides better compression and broad browser support, keeping font payloads small and page performance high in production.
common_pattern: Web font payload/performance management: limiting which font weights ship site-wide and shipping them in an efficient production format. Both generalizations target reducing font asset weight/size for page performance.

text: For Python 3.10 compatibility, either apply the interim fix from mathiasertl/fabric#57 or replace the `fabric3` dev dependency with `fabric`/`invoke` in `pyproject.toml`.
common_pattern: Handling a deprecated dependency (fabric3) that breaks on a newer Python version by either applying an interim patch or migrating to a maintained alternative.

text: Data migrations must be reversible: supply a `reverse_code` that undoes the data change rather than defaulting to `migrations.RunPython.noop`, and for forward-only `RunSQL` migrations pass a single `migrations.RunSQL.noop` as `reverse_sql`; `noop` is acceptable only when reversal is genuinely impossible or meaningless (e.g. a sibling migration in the same change set removes the model/table).
reason: Reversible migrations keep `manage.py migrate <app> <previous>` working and avoid silently leaving the database in an inconsistent state; using the framework's noop sentinel explicitly documents intentional irreversibility without redundant reverse statements.
common_pattern: Django migration hygiene: migrations committed to the repo should represent the final, consolidated schema state (no leftover temporary artifacts) and should express reversibility explicitly and correctly.

text: Keep comments in settings/configuration files accurate and useful: remove or adapt comments that reference deployment details, client apps, or hosting platforms not used by the project; add brief inline comments above non-obvious overrides explaining their purpose and environment scope (e.g., local-only, dev-only).
reason: Prevents misleading configuration documentation, reduces confusion for maintainers, and keeps settings self-documenting so it is clear why a setting is overridden and whether it is safe for local development.
common_pattern: Documentation quality in settings/configuration files: comments should be accurate, relevant to the project's actual infrastructure, and clearly explain non-obvious overrides and their scope.

text: Document non-obvious model/admin fields and custom context-building logic with an inline comment, docstring, or `help_text` explaining their purpose. For Django model and admin fields/configuration, explain why they exist, what depends on them, and when an editor should use them — especially singleton constraints, custom field choices, fields that exist only to support an external or legacy workflow, or fields that override/filter imported/synced data. For non-obvious `get_context` logic, explain why the transformation is performed (e.g., why rows/columns are transposed or data reshaped) and what the resulting context is used for — so future maintainers don't have to reverse-engineer intent.
reason: Non-obvious model attributes, admin fields, and custom context-building logic confuse future maintainers; documenting why they exist, what depends on them, and when an editor or caller should use them reduces the need to reverse-engineer intent.
scope: Django model/admin fields and get_context logic
common_pattern: Django model maintainability: keep model code understandable by documenting non-obvious configuration and separating reusable choice enums into dedicated modules.

text: Write user-facing documentation (README.md and files under docs/) in an impersonal, imperative second-person voice using plain, idiomatic, unambiguous language. Describe actions as direct instructions (e.g., 'run this command in your terminal'); avoid first-person narrative ('I used', 'I ran'), first-person possessives ('my terminal'), uncertain/informal phrasing ('seems to', 'you will have to'), personal/tutorial-style storytelling, 'firstly' (prefer 'first'), and ambiguous constructions (e.g., 'on possibly your editor'); prefer clear grammatical phrasing (e.g., 'which is likely in ...'). Reserve personalized tutorial style for actual tutorials. Keep README command sections concise and command-focused: use direct imperative phrasing for required steps and subject-first phrasing for optional tooling, avoiding second-person 'you can' constructions and dense prose.
reason: Documentation is read by all users, not the author; imperative, reader-focused instructions read like a recipe, are easier to follow and scan, and remain valid regardless of any single contributor's environment. Plain, grammatically clear wording further improves readability, maintains a natural tone, and reduces confusion for users following manual instructions.
scope: user-facing documentation (README.md and docs/), especially README command sections
common_pattern: Documentation voice and tone: user-facing docs (README.md, docs/) should be written in an impersonal, imperative/second-person style that directly instructs any reader, rather than in first-person narrative that describes the author's personal environment or workflow.

text: In README setup/usage instructions and developer docs, explicitly state prerequisites (required local CLI tools, exact access/permission level, platform family) separately from commands, and for every command step state its execution context (local terminal or exact container/service, e.g. 'Docker Desktop terminal'); verify each documented command actually runs in that context, making container-scoped steps directly executable by preferring `docker compose run <service> <command>`, including the exact shell-entry command when a shell is needed, and documenting container-only constraints or providing a `docker compose run` equivalent.
reason: Users otherwise run commands without needed tools, permissions, or platform context, and may run container-only commands in the wrong terminal (e.g., psql, pg_restore), causing avoidable setup failures and manual context switching.
scope: documentation, README setup/usage instructions, Docker-related setup instructions
common_pattern: README/setup documentation for command instructions must be explicit, concise, and current; the cluster contains three complementary sub-patterns: prerequisite clarity, command-section style, and deployment accuracy.

text: When a version is declared via a variable/ARG (e.g. `ARG POETRY_VERSION`), keep every versioned command, URL, or snippet in accompanying comments/documentation synchronized with that same version string.
reason: Stale version references mislead developers and can cause copied commands to install a different version than the image is built with.
common_pattern: Docker/container image and dependency version pinning must be consistent and intentional — pin to an explicit, currently-supported release; align local compose images with deployed environments; and keep version references (tags, ARGs, comments) synchronized. The cluster mixes several distinct-but-related version-hygiene sub-patterns rather than one single principle.

text: Avoid internal/private or vendor-specific links (e.g., private wikis, intranet pages, internal boards) in code comments, configuration, and documentation; move necessary context to a repository wiki or other contributor-accessible location. If a documentation link to an internal resource is required, use a stable redirect/shortlink URL rather than a deep intranet URL so intranet reorganization does not break it.
reason: Internal links are inaccessible to outside contributors, reduce portability/readability, and deep intranet URLs can break when pages are reorganized.
common_pattern: Handling links to internal/private resources in shared code, configuration, and documentation so external contributors are not given inaccessible or unstable references.

text: In documentation, use accurate, specific, and correctly capitalized names in headings and references: use official project/product/tool names and proper-noun capitalization, and avoid generic headings when an owning team or organization should be identified.
reason: This captures the shared principle across project/domain names, product names like Docker, proper nouns like Heroku, and runbook headings that should identify the owning team instead of being generic.
common_pattern: Documentation headings and references should use accurate, specific, correctly capitalized official names; generic or outdated naming should be avoided, especially when ownership can be identified.

text: Proofread all prose—comments, docstrings, and documentation—for typos, duplicate words, and grammatical errors before committing; written text is permanent documentation for future readers and errors erode clarity and professionalism.
reason: This merges both generalizations (comments/docstrings and docs prose) into a single proofreading discipline, since both express the same underlying principle: text authored in a PR becomes lasting documentation and must be clean.
common_pattern: Both generalizations require proofreading written text (comments, docstrings, docs) to catch typos, duplicate words, and grammatical errors, treating prose as permanent, user-facing documentation whose quality affects readability and professionalism.

text: When a model field already defines a default value that pre-populates its initial value, do not add help_text claiming that leaving the field blank will use that default.
reason: The default appears as the initial value, and a blank submission remains blank rather than falling back to the default, so such help_text is misleading.
common_pattern: Django model field attributes (blank, default, help_text) should accurately reflect the field's intended requiredness and default behavior to avoid misleading documentation and invalid form submissions.

text: In user-facing help/documentation, describe actions generically rather than hard-coding exact admin navigation paths or UI labels, and for non-obvious tools or UI actions include a brief reason and a link to the authoritative documentation.
reason: Generic wording keeps help text accurate as UI changes, while rationale and links help users understand and correctly perform non-obvious steps.
common_pattern: User-facing help/documentation should be maintainable and actionable: avoid brittle UI-specific instructions, and explain non-obvious steps with rationale and authoritative links.

text: For Django model fields, set an explicit human-readable `verbose_name` rather than relying on auto-generated labels; capitalize acronyms correctly (e.g., `cta` → `CTA`) and keep labels of related fields consistent in style. Follow the project's existing i18n convention for model labels—do not wrap model labels/verbose names in `gettext_lazy` unless translation is applied consistently across comparable parts of the project.
reason: Auto-generated verbose names mangle acronyms and obscure intent, while inconsistent translation support creates uneven i18n coverage.
common_pattern: Django model/admin fields should carry explicit, consistent, and self-documenting metadata: correct human-readable verbose names (including acronym capitalization and project i18n conventions) and help_text/comments for fields whose purpose is not self-evident.

text: Leave existing user-facing template copy (headings, subheadings, `title=` / `{% trans %}` strings) unchanged unless there is a definite defect such as a typo or spelling error; fix such defects before merging.
reason: Prevents unnecessary copy churn and review noise while ensuring incorrect or misspelled user-visible text never ships.
common_pattern: Both generalizations govern the treatment of existing user-facing copy in templates: don't touch approved wording gratuitously, but do fix clearly broken wording (like typos) before merging.

text: In `blocking.js`, stateful toggle buttons must use a dynamic `aria-label` that describes the next action (e.g., 'Change to Dark Theme' / 'Change to Light Theme'), and this label must be initialized on page load as well as updated after the user clicks the toggle.
reason: A static label does not give screen reader users context about what the toggle will do in the current state, and an uninitialized dynamic label is stale or generic until the first interaction.
common_pattern: Accessible labels for stateful toggle controls must be dynamic: they should describe the next action and be initialized on page load as well as updated after user interaction.

text: In Markdown documentation, use link text that clearly describes the destination or purpose (avoid generic text like 'steps', 'here', or 'link') and keep sentence punctuation outside the link, e.g. `[specific steps for Windows](url).` rather than `[steps.](url)`.
reason: Improves accessibility by making link purpose clear to users and assistive technology, and keeps punctuation out of linked text for cleaner semantics and more predictable screen-reader output.
common_pattern: Accessible Markdown link authoring: descriptive link text and correct punctuation placement.

text: Deployment documentation in README.md should describe the current automated deployment process—including hosting provider and branch-to-environment mapping—and remove stale manual deployment commands.
reason: Keeps contributor documentation accurate and avoids confusion about how deployment is actually performed.
common_pattern: README/setup documentation for command instructions must be explicit, concise, and current; the cluster contains three complementary sub-patterns: prerequisite clarity, command-section style, and deployment accuracy.

text: Template comments should add non-obvious context for readers: do not restate self-documenting code (e.g. `{# title #}` above `{% if page.title %}`) or narrate alternatives that weren't used; write comments for non-developers describing the user-visible behavior and documenting only special cases that can actually occur.
reason: Template comment content is the dominant pattern across PRs #205, #212 and #236 — redundant, implementation-focused, or unreachable-case comments add noise, while comments describing the rendered behavior help designers and content editors follow the logic.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the content and syntax of comments in (Django) templates: comments should earn their place by adding non-obvious, audience-appropriate context rather than restating code, and should use template comment syntax that is stripped from output.

text: When a template or component is reused by another template beyond its own original call site, add a comment in the reused template listing where else it is used (e.g., sibling templates under `cards/`).
reason: Reused templates are easy to break accidentally; documenting extra usage sites signals ripple effects to maintainers and prevents regressions.
common_pattern: Template/component reuse discipline in a design-system-driven Django template project: prefer reusing existing shared includes/component templates over duplicating markup, extend existing components (variants/parameters or sibling components) rather than forking or inlining, and document templates that are reused beyond their original call site.

text: When a Wagtail block's documented behavior (e.g. `ListBlock` item limits) is ambiguous or incomplete, update the block reference documentation to state the supported options (e.g. `max_num`) clearly so authors don't resort to workarounds.
reason: Ambiguous docs led an author to choose a less appropriate block type; accurate docs prevent future misuse.
common_pattern: Wagtail-specific authoring conventions for page models and block fields (class-body organization, documented constraints, generic field/message naming, correct block arguments, and accurate docs).

text: For optional singleton settings lookups that may legitimately have no instance, use `Model.objects.first()` rather than `.get()` or direct singleton access (which raise `DoesNotExist`), and guard against a `None`/falsy return so consumers such as Wagtail context modifiers can skip the absent setting or provide defaults.
reason: .first() returns None when no row exists, letting context modifiers and similar consumers handle missing optional configuration without raising an exception.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail queryset idiom: use `.first()` (optionally with the walrus operator) to fetch and existence-check an object in a single query, and handle the `None`/falsy result safely when the row may legitimately be absent.

text: In Django/Wagtail template tags or context processors that read optional settings from context, access them defensively: follow the `wagtailio/project_styleguide/pattern_contexts.py` pattern, wrap lookups in `try/except (KeyError, AttributeError)` where appropriate, guard against `None` before nested attribute or related-manager access, and on missing/unconfigured settings return the tag's initialized default context (e.g. `menus = []`) rather than an empty `{}` so templates always receive a consistent context shape.
reason: Optional settings may be unconfigured or explicitly `None`; direct indexing or unguarded nested access can crash page rendering, while returning the initialized default context keeps template expectations stable.
scope: project/Wagtail template tags and context processors
common_pattern: Safe and consistent handling of Wagtail/Django template settings and context: settings values should be environment/config-backed rather than hardcoded, manually injected settings should mirror `{% get_settings %}` shape, and optional settings in template tags/context processors should be read defensively with stable fallback context.

text: User-facing validation error messages must be descriptive and suggest corrective action (avoid generic internal identifiers like class names), and when a message convention is updated, apply it consistently to all analogous validation messages in the same module.
reason: Generic messages such as 'Validation error in <Class>' give users no guidance, and fixing only one instance leaves similar blocks with inconsistent, unhelpful errors.
common_pattern: User-facing validation error messages should be descriptive, actionable, and applied consistently across analogous validation sites rather than fixed one at a time.

text: Do not define static class-level flags on Wagtail `Page` subclasses (e.g. `is_preview = False`) to represent runtime state; preview mode is determined at request/serve time, so such attributes are unreachable and misleading.
reason: A hardcoded class attribute can never reflect runtime preview state and makes branches that check it dead code.
common_pattern: Wagtail-specific authoring conventions for page models and block fields (class-body organization, documented constraints, generic field/message naming, correct block arguments, and accurate docs).

text: For fire-and-forget outbound deploy-hook or webhook requests whose response is unused, use a negligible timeout, execute the request synchronously rather than in a background thread, and explicitly catch the timeout exception so it does not break the triggering request.
reason: Waiting for an unused response adds unnecessary latency and complexity, while a negligible timeout will often raise and must be handled deliberately.
common_pattern: Handling outbound fire-and-forget deploy-hook/webhook requests when the timeout is negligible and the response is unused: avoid unnecessary threading or waiting, and explicitly handle the expected timeout exception.

text: When making external HTTP requests with the `requests` library, always pass a `timeout`, use `response.raise_for_status()` instead of manually checking `response.ok`, and wrap the request in a `try/except` for request exceptions such as timeouts and connection errors.
reason: This prevents requests from hanging indefinitely, converts non-OK HTTP responses into exceptions with response context for debugging/Sentry, and ensures network-level failures are handled explicitly instead of producing unhandled tracebacks.
common_pattern: Defensive error handling for external HTTP requests made with the Python `requests` library: enforce a timeout, surface non-OK responses via exceptions, and handle network-level exceptions explicitly.

text: In `StructBlock.clean()`, raise `StructBlockValidationError` (not plain `ValidationError`) with a dict mapping field names to `ErrorList` values — e.g. `raise StructBlockValidationError(block_errors={'field': ErrorList(['...'])})` — and use a `non_field_errors` key for cross-field validations. Plain `ValidationError` is silently swallowed by the struct/stream block machinery, so the error never reaches the user.
reason: Wagtail's StructBlock error API only surfaces `StructBlockValidationError`; other `ValidationError` subclasses do not propagate, and the error payload must be per-field `ErrorList` dict values so errors render against the correct fields.
common_pattern: Both generalizations describe the same Wagtail StructBlock validation-error API: how to raise validation errors inside `StructBlock.clean()`. Generalization 1 covers the exception *type* (`StructBlockValidationError`, not plain `ValidationError`), and Generalization 2 covers the *payload shape* (dict of `{field_name: ErrorList([...])}` with a `non_field_errors` key for cross-field errors). These are complementary halves of one rule, not distinct patterns.

text: Wrap multi-step, related database writes (e.g., repeated `update_or_create` calls plus M2M `add` calls, or any processing loop that performs several related writes) in a single `django.db.transaction.atomic` block, so a failure partway through — such as an exception from a later API request or write — rolls back all writes from that run rather than leaving partial or inconsistent data.
reason: Processing functions often make many external API requests and multiple related model writes; without a transaction, an exception mid-process leaves the database in an inconsistent partial state. Atomic wrapping guarantees all-or-nothing updates.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same principle: multi-step, related Django database writes (repeated `update_or_create` calls plus M2M `add` calls) should be wrapped in `django.db.transaction.atomic` so that a mid-process failure rolls back all writes instead of persisting partial/inconsistent data.

text: In Wagtail, define `search_fields` so that every user-facing content field that should be searchable (e.g., `body`, `intro`, `fine_print`) has an `index.SearchField`; add newly introduced content fields to `search_fields` when they are added to the model, and ensure each field appears only once by removing accidental duplicate `index.SearchField` entries.
reason: Site search should cover all relevant page content, and duplicate search field registrations are redundant and can cause unnecessary indexing/search work or confusing duplicate results.
common_pattern: Maintenance of the Wagtail `search_fields` list on page models: ensuring complete content coverage (index every user-facing field, including newly added ones) and correct/duplicate-free entries.

text: When defining Wagtail admin `panels`, only include panel options that are both supported by the project's pinned Wagtail version and effective in the given field/model context. Omit options unsupported on the pinned version, and don't copy no-op options (e.g., `classname="collapsible"`) from other models where they have no effect.
reason: Keeps the admin upgrade-compatible and avoids dead configuration and misleading admin behavior, since copied panel settings may not apply to a different field type, model, or framework version.
common_pattern: Best practices for defining and customizing Wagtail admin panels: use only version-supported options, avoid no-op options, and extend panels safely via models or hooks.

text: Do not monkey-patch Wagtail's shared `Page.content_panels` / `promote_panels` lists at import time; apply panel customizations on project-specific page models or via the appropriate Wagtail hook instead.
reason: Mutating shared framework definitions in place is fragile, has global side effects, and is hard to reason about; page-model overrides and hooks are the supported extension points.
common_pattern: Best practices for defining and customizing Wagtail admin panels: use only version-supported options, avoid no-op options, and extend panels safely via models or hooks.

text: In `settings/base.py`, read environment-dependent or sensitive configuration (credentials, secrets, external service IDs, feature toggles, third-party API keys, account/newsletter IDs) from environment variables via `env.get("ENV_VAR", default)` rather than hardcoding literals, and always provide a sensible fallback default instead of allowing the value to be `None`. Store environment/deployment-specific values in Django settings or environment variables, never as per-record model/CMS fields. Pass third-party service values through the global template context; never hardcode them as literal arguments inside template `include` tags. When manually adding settings to a template context, use the same nested `settings['<app_label>']['<ModelName>']` shape as `{% get_settings %}` and fetch each settings object once.
reason: Allows configuration and secrets to vary by environment or deployment without code changes, PRs, or redeploys; prevents secrets from being committed or leaked; avoids misconfiguration or runtime errors when a variable is missing; keeps settings consistent with the existing env-driven and `get_settings` patterns; and prevents drift/accidental edits in records as well as duplicate queries in templates.
scope: Django settings and Wagtail templates/template tags
common_pattern: Environment-dependent and sensitive configuration in Django `settings/base.py` should be sourced from environment variables (not hardcoded literals or per-record model/CMS fields), with sensible fallback defaults and descriptive setting names.

text: When a project is derived from an upstream project that publishes canonical shared configs (e.g., Wagtail's ESLint/Prettier/EditorConfig/Stylelint presets such as `stylelint-config-wagtail`), reuse or extend that official shared config in the relevant config file (e.g., `.stylelintrc.js`) rather than an unrelated, legacy, or one-off local config such as `.prettierrc.toml`. Only include project-specific entries such as `ignoreAtRules` for frameworks/at-rules the project actually uses, and remove stale references to unused tools like Tailwind.
reason: Keeps linting, formatting, and editor behavior aligned with the upstream/organizational standards, avoids dead or misleading configuration for unused frameworks, and centralizes config maintenance.
scope: configuration files for upstream-derived projects (Stylelint, ESLint, Prettier, EditorConfig)
common_pattern: Stylelint configuration should remain aligned with the project's canonical preset and reflect actual project usage, rather than carrying stale preset references, unused-framework ignore rules, or inline rule suppressions.

text: In Dockerfiles, minimize image layers by combining related instructions: copy multiple files with the same destination using a single COPY instruction, and chain related RUN commands with `&&` while deleting temporary files within the same RUN layer before it completes.
reason: Fewer Dockerfile instructions produce fewer image layers, reducing final image size. Temporary files must be removed in the same RUN layer they are created in, otherwise they remain in the image.
common_pattern: Minimize Docker image layers by consolidating related Dockerfile instructions into fewer layers.

text: When defining a non-root application user in a Dockerfile for development, create the user with a home directory (e.g. `useradd -m`) and expose a configurable UID build argument used in `useradd -u $UID`, so bind-mounted files created inside the container are owned by the host user. The project's Makefile `setup` target should set that UID for the app container.
reason: Prevents root-owned files in mounted development volumes and lets the non-root container user install packages and customize files such as `.bashrc`.
common_pattern: Development Docker containers should define a non-root application user in a way that supports host-mounted volumes: create a home directory and allow the container user's UID to match the host user, typically via a configurable build argument.

text: Keep local `docker-compose.yml` service image versions aligned with the versions used in staging/production (e.g. `postgres:13` to match staging's 13.6); do not blanket-downgrade infrastructure images as part of unrelated changes.
reason: Version parity prevents dev/test environments from drifting from staging and avoids testing against older, unsupported database behavior.
common_pattern: Docker/container image and dependency version pinning must be consistent and intentional — pin to an explicit, currently-supported release; align local compose images with deployed environments; and keep version references (tags, ARGs, comments) synchronized. The cluster mixes several distinct-but-related version-hygiene sub-patterns rather than one single principle.

text: Add dev-only Django apps to INSTALLED_APPS in environment-specific settings such as dev.py, not in base settings. If a dev-only app must be placed in base INSTALLED_APPS, move its package into the main dependency group.
reason: Keeps development-only packages out of production installations/runtime and aligns INSTALLED_APPS scope with dependency grouping.
common_pattern: Django app registration and configuration: AppConfig naming, custom AppConfig registration via INSTALLED_APPS, default_auto_field handling, and environment-specific INSTALLED_APPS placement.

text: In Docker Compose development configurations, configure services for manual developer workflows without requiring `docker-compose up`: use a no-op keep-alive command (e.g., `tail -f /dev/null`) instead of auto-starting the application server, and preserve service `healthcheck` definitions so one-off management commands can wait for dependencies to become ready.
reason: Keeps dev containers alive without launching the app, allowing developers to start the server manually with custom flags and attach debuggers, while healthchecks let management commands wait for dependencies without a full stack.
common_pattern: Docker Compose development configuration should support developer-controlled workflows (debugging, one-off commands, dependency readiness) instead of forcing the full application stack to auto-start.

text: When scaffolding or editing project metadata files (e.g., `pyproject.toml` `authors`), replace template placeholders such as `"Your Name <you@example.com>"`, empty strings, and `TODO` with real project contact information before committing. For the `wagtailio` project specifically, use `hello@wagtail.org` as the author/contact email.
reason: Placeholder values ship to package indexes and confuse contributors; real project contact (the organization's canonical address) is required for correct package metadata.
common_pattern: Project metadata files must be populated with real project contact information rather than leaving template placeholders, using the organization's canonical contact address (e.g., `hello@wagtail.org`) for wagtailio.

text: Pin the Node.js version in a `.nvmrc` file to the newest LTS release compatible with the project's dependencies, and use that same version when configuring CI and regenerating dependency lockfiles.
reason: Pinning an unnecessarily old Node version, or using a different version in CI than locally, leads to lockfile format/version downgrades, large unintended diffs, and environment drift between local development and CI.
common_pattern: Node.js runtime version consistency: pin it explicitly (via `.nvmrc` to the newest LTS compatible with dependencies) and reuse that pinned version everywhere the toolchain matters — CI and lockfile regeneration — to keep the environment aligned and avoid unintended downgrades.

text: For wagtail.org, declare the browser support policy explicitly: set TypeScript's `compilerOptions.target` to `es2020` in `tsconfig.json` with a comment noting modern-browser support, and define `browserslist` in `package.json` using Wagtail's standard list (Firefox ESR, last 2 Chrome/ChromeAndroid/Edge versions, last 1 Firefox, last 2 iOS, last 3 Safari, excluding Safari 13 and IE 11).
reason: Aligns emitted JavaScript and frontend tooling with a consistent, intentionally chosen browser baseline rather than drifting into legacy targets.
common_pattern: Explicitly declare the project's browser support baseline across TypeScript and frontend build configuration files.

text: Maintain a Makefile in public/contributor-facing projects as a convenience entrypoint for common tasks; keep it updated (with a default target like `help` that lists available commands) even when introducing another task runner.
reason: Makefiles are widely understood and lower the barrier for contributors who may not use or know the preferred tool; a default target improves discoverability and prevents bare `make` from doing nothing or running an unintended target.
common_pattern: Maintaining a user-friendly, discoverable Makefile as a contributed entrypoint for common project tasks, even when adopting other task runners.

text: Configure CI to run code-quality checks and production build on pushes to main and pull requests, and centralize linting/formatting tooling through pre-commit: run hooks via the pre-commit action in CI and manage tool versions in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, rather than defining separate per-tool CI jobs or declaring those tools as development dependencies in `pyproject.toml`.
reason: Ensures CI and local development use the same checks, avoids duplicated CI setup and version management, and keeps lint/format tooling consistent.
common_pattern: Centralize linting/formatting tooling through pre-commit and run code-quality checks in CI, using pre-commit as the single source of truth for tool configuration/versions instead of duplicated per-tool CI jobs or development-dependency declarations.

text: Wrap component includes that depend on optional external configuration in an `{% if %}` guard so they render only when the required settings are present.
reason: Prevents rendering a broken or empty component when the backing service is not configured in a given environment.
common_pattern: Refactoring template conditional logic: consolidating duplicated/over-complex branch conditions and simplifying them by moving resolution into a single normalized context flag or model property, so a template condition reads one source of truth.

text: Keep deployment/environment constants in `fabfile.py` (e.g., `PRODUCTION_APP_INSTANCE`) in sync with the current production application name whenever infrastructure is renamed. When the production app instance is renamed, update the hardcoded value (currently `"wagtail-org-production"`).
reason: Prevents deployment scripts from targeting a stale or nonexistent app instance.
common_pattern: Both generalizations address the same issue: the `PRODUCTION_APP_INSTANCE` constant in `fabfile.py` is a hardcoded deployment target that must be updated whenever the production infrastructure (app instance) is renamed. Generalization 1 states the principle; Generalization 2 is the concrete instance-specific fix. This is a clear convergence (principle + its entity-specific instantiation).

text: Component preview and fixture artifacts (e.g., styleguide/pattern-library templates and YAML fixtures) should use explicit sizing that matches the design specification, avoiding clipping or approximate dimensions that cause review discrepancies.
reason: Ensures design and implementation reviews show the component as designed, not cropped or visually inaccurate due to default viewport sizing or approximated fixture dimensions.
scope: project pattern library/styleguide templates and component fixtures, especially streamfield/card template YAML
common_pattern: Component preview and fixture artifacts should use explicit sizing that matches the design specification, so reviewers see an accurate, unclipped representation of the component.

text: When a StreamField or StructBlock already exposes a `required` value, use that configured value to determine requiredness rather than adding custom helper methods.
reason: Avoids duplicated requiredness logic, keeps the requirement defined in one place, and relies on the framework's built-in behavior.
common_pattern: Block-level validation for optional/alternative fields in Wagtail StructBlock/StreamField blocks, plus reuse of existing required configuration instead of custom requiredness logic.

text: When adding or configuring a third-party GitHub Action that requires secrets or privileged operations (e.g., `calibreapp/image-actions`), follow the vendor's documented combined-workflow pattern with separate unprivileged/privileged jobs for fork PRs rather than using a custom split workflow or a same-repository guard.
reason: Forked PRs do not receive repository secrets or write permissions, so privileged steps fail; the upstream combined-workflow pattern safely handles both same-repo and forked PR scenarios without reimplementing the fork limitation workaround.
common_pattern: Maintaining GitHub Actions workflows by keeping action versions current and following vendor-documented integration patterns for privileged/forked-PR scenarios.

text: In the wagtailio project, do not use Django i18n translation tags ({%% trans %%}, {%% blocktrans %%}, {%% load i18n %%}) in templates because the site is not localized; however, keep USE_L10N = True in wagtailio/settings/base.py until Django is upgraded to 4.1 or later (where it becomes the default).
reason: The wagtail.io site is not localized, so translation tags add unnecessary indirection, but format localization (USE_L10N) is still needed for the current Django version used by the project.
common_pattern: i18n/l10n configuration policy for the wagtailio project

text: Configure the frontend build to emit hashed bundle filenames and configure the Django manifest loader (e.g., `django-manifest-loader`) to point at the Webpack manifest, with appropriate development and production behavior.
reason: Required for the manifest loader to map logical asset names to the hashed filenames generated by the frontend build, enabling reliable cache invalidation.
scope: project frontend build and Django settings
common_pattern: Use a manifest loader for compiled frontend assets in Django templates instead of direct {% static %} paths, with supporting Webpack/Django configuration for hashed filenames.

text: Register a custom Django AppConfig by adding its dotted path to INSTALLED_APPS rather than setting default_app_config in the app's __init__.py. Use default_app_config only for legacy Django versions if explicitly required.
reason: default_app_config is deprecated/discouraged; explicit INSTALLED_APPS configuration is the current Django-recommended approach.
common_pattern: Django app registration and configuration: AppConfig naming, custom AppConfig registration via INSTALLED_APPS, default_auto_field handling, and environment-specific INSTALLED_APPS placement.

text: Set project-wide Django defaults such as DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD once in the shared base settings module. In AppConfig classes, set default_auto_field only for apps that define models; omit it for apps without models.
reason: Centralizing project-wide settings avoids duplication, while per-app default_auto_field is only meaningful when the app contains models.
common_pattern: Django app registration and configuration: AppConfig naming, custom AppConfig registration via INSTALLED_APPS, default_auto_field handling, and environment-specific INSTALLED_APPS placement.

text: When invalidating a Django template fragment cache manually (e.g., from a model's `save()`), pass exactly the same `vary_on` dimensions used by the corresponding `{% cache %}` template tag, including request-dependent flags like `request.is_preview`. For boolean vary dimensions, clear the non-preview/committed variant (e.g., `False`) and invalidate every variant that could be served. Include known variation dimensions such as preview mode upfront when caching is first introduced, rather than retrofitting them after the related preview feature ships.
reason: Fragment cache keys are derived from the fragment name plus `vary_on`; a mismatch silently targets a different key and leaves stale or viewer-specific content cached. Adding these dimensions at caching time avoids cache-sharing bugs later.
common_pattern: Correct construction and matching of Django template fragment cache keys — the `vary_on` dimensions used when rendering a `{% cache %}` fragment must be mirrored exactly when invalidating, and the right key-builder utility must be chosen based on whether the fragment varies on a specific page instance.

text: When configuring Wagtail RichText fields or StreamField rich-text blocks, enable rich text only where formatting is actually required and always pass an explicit minimal `features` allowlist of valid Wagtail feature names (e.g. `p`, `a`, `ul`, `li`, `link`, `document`) rather than allowing headings or full formatting; do not use raw HTML tags like `br` as feature names, and use a plain text block/field (e.g. `CharBlock`) instead of a rich-text field where only plain text is needed.
reason: Wagtail rich-text fields validate feature identifiers and cannot render markup a TextField/plain block was never meant to hold; restricting features to the approved minimal set avoids invalid feature names, unintended formatting, and bespoke front-end handling for unsupported elements like headings.
scope: Wagtail page models and StreamField block definitions
common_pattern: Wagtail rich-text handling: how RichText fields should be configured (restrictive feature allowlists, RichText vs CharBlock choice) and how their values should be rendered in templates (|richtext filter, block-level <div> wrapper, |striptags for plain text).

text: Prefer names that identify the specific domain concept or structural role of a class, method, or property over generic or inherited terms; for example, use `is_link_required` instead of `is_required`, and `RoadmapItem` or `MilestoneItem` instead of `Item`. Similarly, environment-backed credential settings in `settings/base.py` should be named to denote their specific purpose or scope, rather than using generic names like `{SERVICE}_ACCESS_TOKEN`.
reason: Generic names force developers to trace into superclasses or surrounding code to understand intent, while domain- and role-specific names are self-documenting. For credentials, a descriptive setting name clarifies what the token is for, which is especially important for fine-grained tokens scoped to specific permissions or integrations.
common_pattern: All generalizations advocate replacing generic or inherited/reused names with names that identify the specific domain concept or structural role, improving self-documentation and readability.

text: Name reusable components, templates, and model/component attributes after the generic content role or request behavior they represent, not incidental visual/implementation details or specific frontend libraries. For StreamField components, use role-based class names like `VideoBlock` rather than `LoopingVideoBlock`, and name reusable card block templates in `patterns/components/streamfields/cards/` for their generic card role rather than a specific visual element like `logo_card_block`; when renaming or moving such a template, update all `{% include %}` references and related card template paths (e.g., `card_list_block.html`). For attributes that select a fragment template for partial requests, name them after the generic request behavior (e.g., `ajax_template`) rather than a specific library (e.g., `htmx_template`), keeping the model and public API decoupled from frontend implementation details.
reason: Content- and role-based names improve discoverability and reuse across features, while updating all references prevents broken template includes and stale path references. Similarly, request-behavior-based attribute names keep the model and public API decoupled from frontend implementation details, so switching libraries does not force a rename.
scope: global (with project-specific StreamField component/template naming examples)
common_pattern: Maintaining reusable card block templates: generic naming for reuse and updating all references when renaming or moving.

text: Avoid embedding organization domain TLD suffixes (e.g. `io`) in project identifiers such as database names, database users, Django settings modules, service names, and docker-compose references; prefer the current domain or a domain-neutral project name (for Wagtail, use `wagtail` instead of `wagtailio`).
reason: Prevents stale branding and avoids renaming identifiers throughout the project when the organization's domain changes.
common_pattern: Avoid embedding organization/domain-specific TLD suffixes (e.g. `.io`) in project identifiers to prevent stale branding and future rename churn after domain migrations.

text: Use fully spelled-out, correctly spelled, descriptive variable names — even for short-lived locals. Avoid abbreviations (`curr_row` → `current_row`) and avoid single-letter names like `e`, which conventionally denotes an exception variable (`except Exception as e`).
reason: Abbreviated or misspelled identifiers reduce readability, break grep/search, and can silently propagate via copy-paste; misleading names like `e` cause confusion by colliding with established conventions.
common_pattern: All three generalizations enforce identifier naming quality for readability: avoid abbreviations, avoid misleading single-letter names (especially `e` which connotes exceptions), and ensure correct spelling. They converge on 'variable names must be self-explanatory and unambiguous'.

text: Name pattern/component template directories and files descriptively and consistently: use snake_case for component directory/template names under `patterns/components/`, align template pattern directory names with related Sass/style paths (e.g. `patterns/atoms/icons/` with `static/sass/atoms/icons.scss`), choose names that reflect the specific content or purpose they render, and split semantically distinct variants into separate templates (e.g. `button.html` for `<button>` vs. `button-link.html` for anchors styled as buttons) rather than overloading one include.
reason: Consistent naming across templates and styles improves discoverability, reduces ambiguity, and preserves clear distinctions between semantically different components.
common_pattern: Consistent, descriptive naming for component/template directories and files, aligned with existing project conventions and the rendered content/semantic purpose.

text: For Wagtail models registered with `@register_snippet`, omit the `Snippet` suffix from the class name and use the plain domain name (e.g., `FooterMenu`, `MainMenu`, `MainMenuItem`).
reason: The `@register_snippet` decorator already communicates that the model is a snippet, so adding `Snippet` to the class name is redundant and makes names longer without adding information.
common_pattern: Choose the appropriate Wagtail model construct for content modeling based on editing needs and required features, and follow naming conventions for snippets.

text: Name private model helper methods that return a computed collection as `_get_<noun>()` rather than `_filter_<noun>()` when the method primarily retrieves data; reserve `filter` naming for methods that actually filter a queryset/collection by criteria.
reason: The method name communicates intent at call sites and avoids reading like a side-effecting action when it is mainly a getter.
common_pattern: Model-level helper methods (Django model helpers) should be pure data getters: name them as getters and keep UI/presentation concerns (like 'All' sentinel values) out of the model layer.

text: Name Django AppConfig subclasses in apps.py using CamelCase with a Config suffix matching the app/package name, consistent with the project's model class naming.
reason: Follows Django/Python class naming conventions and keeps AppConfig names consistent with the rest of the project.
common_pattern: Django app registration and configuration: AppConfig naming, custom AppConfig registration via INSTALLED_APPS, default_auto_field handling, and environment-specific INSTALLED_APPS placement.

text: Do not repurpose a field for semantically different content (e.g., using `value.logo` to render an author avatar). Either use a field named for the element being rendered, or extract a dedicated template/component for the distinct variant rather than overloading an existing field.
reason: Field names that don't match what they render are misleading and make templates harder to reason about; similar-but-distinct variants are clearer as separate templates or clearly-named fields.
common_pattern: Frontend templates must render semantically correct content: fields should be named for what they actually represent, and templates should only output user-facing content (not structural/CMS-only values).

text: When modeling content in Wagtail, choose the simplest construct that meets the content's needs. For a single, fixed media attachment (image/video), use a `ForeignKey` to the media model exposed via the matching chooser panel (e.g. `VideoChooserPanel`) in `content_panels`; do not use a `StreamField` for a single fixed media item. Use `StreamField` for repeatable or editor-arranged content blocks (e.g., CTAs) instead of fixed fields; use snippets for content that needs staging or preview rather than large settings models with `StreamField`s; and default to plain `models.Model` unless `ClusterableModel` is required for parent/child or snippet-chooser relationships.
reason: A chooser panel provides a dedicated media-selection UI, a ForeignKey enforces single-value semantics, and StreamField is reserved for flexible/repeatable content. More generally, selecting the simplest appropriate Wagtail construct avoids over-engineering, gives editors flexibility, supports staging/preview workflows, and reduces unnecessary framework coupling.
common_pattern: Choose the appropriate Wagtail model construct for content modeling based on editing needs and required features, and follow naming conventions for snippets.

text: When a media chooser block subclass must restrict selection to a specific media type, override its `field` cached property to return a `forms.ModelChoiceField` with `queryset=self.target_model.objects.filter(type="<media_type>")`, passing through `widget`, `required`, `validators`, and `help_text` from the base block.
reason: Enforces the media-type restriction at the field level while preserving the base block's widget, validation, required, and help-text behavior.
common_pattern: Both generalizations prescribe how to model media selection in Wagtail page/section blocks: prefer chooser-based fields (ForeignKey + chooser panel, or a filtered ModelChoiceField via the `field` property) over generic content containers, and enforce the intended media type at the field/queryset level.

text: For model fields representing selectable icons or emojis, store stable string identifiers (e.g., CLDR short names like "thumbs up") as the choice value rather than raw UTF-8 emoji characters, and let the front end map those identifiers to emoji glyphs or image assets.
reason: Decoupling stored values from their visual representation keeps rendering flexible, ensures consistent display across browsers and devices, and avoids encoding/presentation concerns leaking into the data model.
common_pattern: Storing selectable icon/emoji values as stable string identifiers (CLDR short names) instead of raw Unicode characters, deferring rendering to the front end.

text: Content page models with a heading should include an optional `intro = RichTextField(blank=True)` field to provide introductory copy below the heading, matching the convention used by other page models.
reason: Keeps editor and developer expectations consistent across page models and gives editors a standard, optional way to add introductory text.
common_pattern: Wagtail rich-text handling: how RichText fields should be configured (restrictive feature allowlists, RichText vs CharBlock choice) and how their values should be rendered in templates (|richtext filter, block-level <div> wrapper, |striptags for plain text).

text: When defining Wagtail Page models, reuse existing project mixins (e.g., SocialMediaMixin, HeroMixin) for shared fields and behavior instead of reimplementing them. Validation for mixin-provided fields belongs in the mixin itself, not duplicated in each model's clean(). If a model intentionally moves away from a mixin, migrate any still-needed fields directly into the model rather than partially inheriting from it.
reason: This rule consolidates best practices: reuse mixins to avoid duplication and inconsistency, keep shared validation in the mixin, and eliminate partial inheritance by fully migrating needed fields when departing from a mixin.
common_pattern: Proper use of project mixins for shared model fields and behavior, avoiding duplication and partial inheritance.

text: Choose Django model field types and `max_length` values to match the actual content: set `CharField.max_length` to the realistic maximum rather than defaulting to 255, account for multi-codepoint unicode/emoji when sizing single-character fields, and use `TextField` (or a multi-line editor widget) for fields intended to store multi-line content such as code snippets.
reason: Oversized length limits misrepresent the field constraint, and single-line `CharField` inputs are inappropriate for multi-line content. Model schema should reflect the real content shape and size.
common_pattern: Django model fields should be configured to match the actual shape and size of the stored data, including field type selection (CharField vs TextField) and realistic max_length sizing.

text: When defining Django/Wagtail model relationships, choose the field type and options to match actual ownership, cardinality, and domain meaning: use `on_delete=models.CASCADE` for child records owned by a parent page so they do not outlive the parent; use a simple `ForeignKey` unless multiple related objects per instance are genuinely required; and name `related_name` after the specific semantic relationship rather than generic page/model structure.
reason: This merges three tightly related relationship-design subpatterns: (1) G1/G2 converge on CASCADE for page-owned child records; (2) G3/G4 converge on simple ForeignKey unless a true one-to-many relation is required; (3) G5/G6 converge on semantic related_name naming, with G6 being a specific instance of G5. No contradictions are present.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail model relationships should be defined according to the relation's actual ownership, cardinality, and semantic meaning rather than default or generic choices.

text: In Django models, keep the model as the single source of truth: do not store values that can be deterministically computed from existing fields (expose them as @property methods instead), and do not duplicate model-level validation invariants in consuming views or rendering code.
reason: Prevents inconsistent duplicate data, redundant database columns, and validation drift by centralizing derived values and invariants in the model.
common_pattern: Keep the Django model as the single source of truth by avoiding duplicated derived data and duplicated model-level validation logic.

text: When syncing externally sourced records into Django models, use upsert semantics (`update_or_create`) rather than create/delete-only logic so that changes to mutable fields are propagated. Accept the per-record query overhead for small datasets and only switch to batched/bulk strategies if the volume grows large enough to matter.
reason: Create/delete-only sync silently drops updates to mutable fields (e.g. titles), leaving the database stale. The extra per-record queries are acceptable for small datasets, but the rule should be tied to scale rather than treated as universally optimal.
scope: Django data-sync management commands that syncing external API data into local models
common_pattern: Use upsert (update_or_create) when syncing external records into Django models to keep mutable fields in sync; accept the per-record query cost for small datasets and only optimize with batching when volume grows.

text: When adding extra values to a page's context inside `get_context()`, merge them with `context.update({...})` instead of the `|=` in-place union operator.
reason: `.update()` is the idiomatic, explicit, and more widely compatible way to merge values into a Django/Wagtail template context; `|=` depends on Python 3.9+ mapping semantics and is less conventional in the codebase.
common_pattern: Conventions for authoring `get_context()` methods on Django/Wagtail blocks — both generalizations target the same method name across different PRs, one addressing how the context-building logic should be documented and the other addressing how the resulting context should be merged. They share the entity (`get_context`) but are genuinely distinct concerns (documentation vs. merge idiom).

text: When rendering a wagtailmedia `Video` in templates, iterate over the model's `sources` property and emit a `<source>` tag per entry; do not hand-assemble `src`/`type` from `video.type`, `video.file_extension`, and `video.url` (those fields do not combine into a valid MIME string).
reason: The `sources` property already exposes the correct per-source `src` and MIME `type` and handles multiple sources/formats; manual reconstruction diverges from the intended interface and produces incorrect markup.
common_pattern: Both generalizations describe the same principle: use the wagtailmedia Video model's `sources` API when rendering video in templates, instead of manually reconstructing source URLs and MIME types from separate model fields (`type`, `file_extension`, `url`).

text: Expose editor-facing boolean options (e.g., a checkbox) for block behaviors that can vary per instance (such as looping); for behaviors that are always enabled or fixed, omit the boolean field and document the fixed behavior in the block/field `help_text` instead.
reason: Editors need control over variations like looping, but exposing options for fixed behavior creates nonsensical configurations and bloats the block API. Documenting fixed behavior makes it explicit in the CMS UI while keeping the API minimal.
common_pattern: How to decide whether to expose a configurable boolean option in specialized media/StructBlocks: expose when behavior varies per instance, omit and document when behavior is fixed.

text: In Wagtail search result templates, when promoted/editor's picks are excluded from the main search results to avoid duplicates, render them separately using `{% get_search_promotions %}` and reuse the standard search result partial; ensure `wagtailsearchpromotions_tags` is loaded so the tag is available.
reason: Promoted content is intentionally removed from the normal result queryset, so it must be rendered explicitly. Reusing the standard partial keeps promoted-result markup consistent with regular results, and Django template tags require their defining library to be loaded.
common_pattern: Correct rendering of Wagtail search promotions when promoted/editor's-picks are excluded from the main search results queryset: the template must render them separately using the Wagtail promotion tag, while also loading the tag library and reusing the standard result partial for consistent markup.

text: For bounded list queries, prefer a single ordered limit (e.g., first N by due date) without conditional state filters or an import_all flag. In `wagtailio/roadmap/views.py`, fetch milestones with `milestones(first: 20, orderBy: {field: DUE_DATE, direction: ASC})` and no `states` argument, removing the `import_all` parameter and conditional `CLOSED` state branch.
reason: Simplifies the query and caller API because the ordered/limited subset already constrains the result set sufficiently.
common_pattern: Both generalizations describe the same simplification: replace conditional status/state filtering and branching on an import-all flag with a single ordered, bounded query that returns the first N items by due date regardless of state.

text: Do not include presentation/UI sentinel values (e.g., an `"All"` choice) in model-level data helpers; return the raw computed collection and add such default/sentinel choices in `get_context()`.
reason: Keeps model helpers focused on data retrieval and prevents consumers like filtering methods from having to account for UI-only values.
common_pattern: Model-level helper methods (Django model helpers) should be pure data getters: name them as getters and keep UI/presentation concerns (like 'All' sentinel values) out of the model layer.

text: When declaring Wagtail `StreamField` fields, omit redundant arguments: do not pass `use_json_field=True` (unnecessary in Wagtail 6.0+) and do not set `null=True` (StreamField defaults to an empty JSON list `[]`; use `blank=True` instead to allow empty input).
reason: Keeps StreamField declarations concise, consistent, and aligned with StreamField's semantics and the installed Wagtail version.
common_pattern: Avoiding redundant or unnecessary keyword arguments in Wagtail StreamField field declarations

text: When defining Wagtail model/snippet admin `panels`, group conceptually related fields into `MultiFieldPanel` sections rather than flat `FieldPanel` lists; give each panel a human-readable heading (append `(read-only)` when the grouped fields are read-only) and use `help_text` to explain editorial constraints or choices; order fields within a panel by the intended authoring flow. Keep content fields separate from external service/credential fields.
reason: Grouped, labeled, and well-ordered panels improve editor usability by separating logically distinct areas, making constraints explicit, and guiding content entry.
common_pattern: Design of Wagtail admin `panels` using `MultiFieldPanel` to group, label, annotate, and order related fields for editor clarity.

text: In templates, keep conditionals tied to a single normalized flag/property exposed from the block, component model, or include call site (e.g. `value.url`, `image_on_right`), rather than checking multiple raw source fields directly. Use that dedicated boolean flag as the sole source of truth for conditional rendering; do not combine it with an ancillary field via `or` or infer display from an incidental URL field, so render conditions stay aligned with the authoritative data.
reason: Centralizes resolution logic, decouples front-end layout logic from raw model field names, and avoids showing incomplete/incorrect UI based on the presence of an ancillary field.
common_pattern: Refactoring template conditional logic: consolidating duplicated/over-complex branch conditions and simplifying them by moving resolution into a single normalized context flag or model property, so a template condition reads one source of truth.

text: Only set `blank=True` (or `required=False`, or use optional blocks) on a model/snippet/content field or block when the design genuinely allows it to be omitted or empty; if the model's intended structure requires a value, omit `blank=True` so Django form validation enforces requiredness. Do not force editors to always supply content that the design intentionally leaves empty, and do not use `blank=True` on required fields where it would allow invalid empty values that contradict the model's semantics.
reason: blank=True controls form-level requiredness; using it on a required field allows invalid empty values that contradict the model's semantics, while forcing content on genuinely optional fields creates validation errors and unnecessary editorial friction.
common_pattern: Editor-facing content fields/blocks should be declared optional (blank=True / required=False, or optional blocks) whenever the design permits omission, rather than forcing content to always be present.

text: When counting usages via Wagtail's ReferenceIndex, deduplicate references with `.values('content_type_id', 'object_id').distinct()` before aggregating `Count`, so multiple references from the same parent object count as one usage.
reason: Prevents inflated usage counts when the same asset is referenced multiple times by the same page or object; the report should count distinct referencing objects, not raw reference rows.
common_pattern: Correct usage counting through Wagtail's ReferenceIndex: deduplicate references per referencing object and ensure the queried content type matches the actual project-specific model.

text: When querying Wagtail's ReferenceIndex for a project-specific model, use the project-specific model class in `ContentType.objects.get_for_model()` rather than the corresponding Wagtail base model.
reason: The content type must match the actual model being reported on; using the base model can cause incorrect or missing matches.
common_pattern: Correct usage counting through Wagtail's ReferenceIndex: deduplicate references per referencing object and ensure the queried content type matches the actual project-specific model.

text: For template fragment cache keys that vary on a specific page instance, prefer the framework (Wagtail) utility that encapsulates the page key-variation logic over calling `make_template_fragment_key` with hand-passed magic values. For page-agnostic fragment caches (e.g., site-level navigation, settings, or pattern-library caches), use Django's `make_template_fragment_key` directly, since the Wagtail page utility requires a page object you don't have.
reason: The framework utility keeps variation logic correct and avoids misleading magic values for page-dependent caches, while the direct Django utility matches the page-agnostic nature of site-wide caches.
common_pattern: Correct construction and matching of Django template fragment cache keys — the `vary_on` dimensions used when rendering a `{% cache %}` fragment must be mirrored exactly when invalidating, and the right key-builder utility must be chosen based on whether the fragment varies on a specific page instance.

text: When defining Wagtail StructBlock/StreamField blocks, follow API design best practices: use generic field names (e.g. `page`) and generic validation messages (e.g. 'You must specify a page or a URL.') rather than names/messages derived from the currently allowed entity type; use block-level arguments such as `required`/`help_text` instead of Django model-field arguments like `null`; and for blocks with multiple optional alternative fields (such as link targets or CTA fields), add block-level `clean()` validation to enforce the intended combinations—require at least one target where a destination is needed, allow at most one alternative where only one may be set, and require companion labels such as CTA `text` when a link target is provided—applying the same validation to sibling block classes that share the same optional link-target layout.
reason: Entity-specific names and messages become misleading when a `PageChooserBlock`'s `page_type` scope later expands; Wagtail block classes may not accept model-field kwargs such as `null` (optionality is expressed via `required`); and block-level `clean()` validation prevents invalid block states, keeps related block types consistent, and surfaces misuse through framework validation instead of allowing invalid saved data.
scope: Wagtail StructBlock/StreamField blocks, especially link/navigation and CTA blocks with optional alternative fields
common_pattern: Block-level validation for optional/alternative fields in Wagtail StructBlock/StreamField blocks, plus reuse of existing required configuration instead of custom requiredness logic.

text: In Django + HTMX projects, use `django-htmx` for HTMX request detection (e.g. `request.htmx`) instead of manually checking the `HX-Request` header. For HTMX partial responses that should update the browser URL/history, set the `HX-Push-Url` response header in the view rather than using inline JavaScript in the fragment template.
reason: These mechanisms centralize HTMX request parsing and URL updates, provide consistent helpers, and avoid duplicated custom logic and inline scripts.
common_pattern: Adopt idiomatic HTMX patterns in Django templates instead of manual header checks, inline JavaScript, or ad-hoc attribute usage.

text: Do not hard-code CTA/link button labels (e.g. 'View docs') in StreamField block templates. Add a separate editable CharBlock field (e.g. `link_title`) to the block and render from it (e.g. `{{ value.link_title }}`), falling back to a sensible default label when the field is empty.
reason: Hard-coded labels are only correct for a single destination; making the button/link title editor-configurable keeps the block reusable for non-docs links and lets editors adapt CTA copy to different designs, while a fallback avoids blank labels.
common_pattern: This cluster mixes two related-but-distinct sub-patterns: (A) consolidating/aligning CTA template files and references with the project's per-directory StreamField template convention, and (B) not hard-coding CTA/link label text in StreamField templates — expose an editor-configurable field with a fallback default. Sub-pattern B is the stronger, tighter convergence (4 generalizations, essentially the same principle rephrased). Sub-pattern A is more project-file-path-specific but still coherent (3 generalizations all pointing at the same CTA template naming/location cleanup).

text: For Wagtail StreamField/StreamBlock rendering, define a template only on the outermost block for nested structures and render each block through its own dedicated block template; parent/page templates should call or include the block rather than iterating child block data or adding inline `{% if block.block_type == ... %}` / `{% elif %}` branches.
reason: The block should own its child rendering logic. Dedicated per-block templates keep markup encapsulated and reusable, avoid duplicated structure, and prevent parent templates from depending on block internals.
scope: Wagtail StreamField/StreamBlock definitions and parent templates
common_pattern: Wagtail StreamField components should be organized and rendered through dedicated per-block templates under `patterns/components/streamfields/`, with correct/current template references, block-owned rendering rather than parent-template inline branching, and removal of confirmed-unused blocks/templates.

text: Keep scripts and assets required on every page out of child-overridable template blocks such as `{% block extra_js %}`. Place global scripts directly in the root `base.html` (or a non-overridable include/block), so child templates cannot silently remove or replace them by overriding the block; conversely, keep page-specific scripts in page-specific templates rather than in shared pattern-library/base page templates.
reason: Blocks like `extra_js` are intended for child customization; putting always-required scripts inside them makes their inclusion fragile because any child override can drop them. Likewise, putting page-only scripts in a shared base template leaks them into pattern-library pages and non-page views (e.g., 404/500).
scope: Django template inheritance / shared base templates
common_pattern: Django template script organization — controlling where JavaScript lives in templates: keeping global scripts outside child-overridable blocks, keeping page-specific scripts out of shared base templates, and extracting inline JS into static files.

text: In `main.js`, only initialize components that are used site-wide. Page-specific component initialization should be extracted into a dedicated page bundle and included from the relevant page template, and any unused `initComponent` calls should be removed from the `DOMContentLoaded` initialization list.
reason: Keeps the global bundle minimal, avoids loading page-specific JavaScript on every page, and prevents dead code and unnecessary runtime logic.
common_pattern: Keep the global `main.js` entry point minimal: avoid page-specific initializations and remove unused ones.
