text: Do not put layout/alignment properties (e.g., `margin: 0 auto`) on shared/base component classes in `wagtailio/static/sass/components/`; keep such overrides in the consuming context (e.g., an inline `<style>` in the matching pattern-library template for pattern-library-only display) or in instance-specific modifiers. Prefer explicit, semantic, component-owned class names over implicit or context-dependent styling: express parent-context variants as BEM modifier classes on the child component (e.g., `icon__svg-bg--{variant}`) or pass them via a `classes` parameter on includes; do not override child styles from parent partials, do not target children with structural selectors such as `> div`, and do not name classes after mutable values (use role-based names). Name a class after its sole owning component (e.g., `.code-block`) rather than a generic layout/utility name (e.g., `.grid-align`), so shared components remain reusable.
reason: Shared components should remain reusable and self-contained: context-specific layout/alignment and parent-context variants belong in the consuming context or explicit component-owned modifiers, not shared base classes or parent partials; semantic component-owned naming and selectors keep styles decoupled from parent structure and maintainable.
scope: wagtailio Sass components, pattern-library templates, and template includes
common_pattern: CSS/Sass layout and spacing conventions for the wagtailio design system: centralizing spacing via shared mixins, aligning components with the page `grid` class, and keeping context-specific alignment overrides out of shared component classes.

text: When making a code change or addressing review feedback, perform closely related cleanup in the same change: apply the same fix to all similar occurrences, remove obsolete files, delete stale inline comments, and remove no-op or dead code. In particular, when a change removes the last reference to a Wagtail template, partial, or static asset—including by changing a page/model `template` attribute or migrating to a new layout—or confirms that a StreamField/StreamBlock child block is unused, delete the now-unused file and block definition in the same change. Do not keep dead code by marking blocks with placeholder groups such as `group="DO NOT USE"` or leaving `# to be removed` comments.
reason: Keeps the codebase tidy and consistent, prevents dead templates/assets and orphaned StreamField block definitions from lingering, avoids confusing editor UI groups and misleading artifacts, and prevents repeated review feedback for the same class of issue.
scope: global (Wagtail templates, partials, static assets, and StreamField/StreamBlock block definitions)
common_pattern: Removing dead template or asset files in the same change that eliminates their last reference, especially after migrations, layout changes, or page/model template attribute updates.

text: Reuse existing shared component/template includes (e.g. `patterns/components/author/author.html`, `patterns/components/icon/icon.html`, `hero.html`, and `patterns/components/streamfields/cta/cta.html`) rather than duplicating, forking, or inlining equivalent markup. When an existing component does not cover a needed case, extend it by adding a parameter/variant (e.g. a `variant` variable) or a sibling component for a different semantic variant. In wagtailio StreamField components under `patterns/components/streamfields/`, give each block its own `{block_name}/` directory containing `{block_name}.html` and its matching `{block_name}.yaml`; avoid duplicate `cta_block.html` / `*_block.html` wrappers, and keep every Wagtail `Meta.template` reference—including nested child block references—pointing to the correct current path.
reason: Centralizing markup in shared components keeps styling, ARIA, and behavior consistent, makes future changes single-point, and avoids similar-but-divergent duplicate templates. In StreamField components, it also keeps each block's HTML and YAML together, scales readably as blocks grow, consolidates CTA rendering, and prevents stale template references from rendering outdated markup.
scope: global; with wagtailio StreamField pattern/component specifics under `patterns/components/streamfields/`
common_pattern: Template/component reuse discipline in a design-system-driven Django template project: prefer reusing existing shared includes/component templates over duplicating markup, extend existing components (variants/parameters or sibling components) rather than forking or inlining, and document templates that are reused beyond their original call site.

text: In SCSS/CSS, avoid duplicating styling: group selectors that share identical declaration blocks into a single comma-separated selector list; remove declarations that merely repeat properties already set by an applicable ancestor selector, an earlier rule in the same file, or the base selector state (e.g., inside :hover). Also do not redeclare a property inside an `@include media-query(...)` block when the same property/value is already applied to that selector outside the media query.
reason: Reduces duplication and noise, keeps shared behavior in one place, avoids source-order/specificity confusion, keeps the cascade easier to reason about, and prevents declarations (including base and responsive values) from drifting out of sync when only one copy is updated.
common_pattern: Avoiding redundant/duplicated styling in SCSS/CSS by consolidating shared selectors and removing declarations already provided by an applicable ancestor, earlier rule, or base selector state.

text: Define TextChoices / enum choice classes in a dedicated `choices.py` module rather than inline inside `models.py`.
reason: Keeps model files focused on model definitions and makes shared choice enums reusable and easier to locate.
common_pattern: Django model maintainability: keep model code understandable by documenting non-obvious configuration and separating reusable choice enums into dedicated modules.

text: Ensure every file (including HTML templates and other text files) ends with a single trailing newline.
reason: Trailing newlines follow standard POSIX text-file conventions, prevent Git 'No newline at end of file' warnings and diff noise, and satisfy common formatters/linters.
common_pattern: Both generalizations require files to end with a trailing newline, differing only in whether they explicitly call out a specific file type (HTML templates) or state the rule globally.

text: When an existence check on a queryset is immediately followed by fetching the same object (e.g. `.exists()` then `.first()`, or a truthiness check then indexing), fetch once and test the fetched value instead — prefer `Model.objects.first()`, and use the walrus operator (`if obj := Model.objects.first():`) to bind the object for use inside the block.
reason: Avoids a redundant database query, prevents `IndexError` on empty querysets, and simplifies control flow by reusing the already-fetched object.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail queryset idiom: use `.first()` (optionally with the walrus operator) to fetch and existence-check an object in a single query, and handle the `None`/falsy result safely when the row may legitimately be absent.

text: In HTML templates, omit attributes that HTML5 already implies: do not write `type="text/css"` on `<link rel="stylesheet">` or `type="text/javascript"` on `<script>` tags.
reason: These attributes are redundant under HTML5, so removing them reduces markup noise and keeps templates aligned with modern conventions.
common_pattern: Removing legacy/redundant markup from shared HTML templates so they reflect modern HTML5 defaults and the project's actual browser-support requirements.

text: When the project no longer supports Internet Explorer, remove IE-specific compatibility markup from base templates, including `<meta http-equiv="x-ua-compatible" content="ie=edge">` and `<!--[if lt IE 9]>` conditional comment blocks.
reason: Dead legacy browser workarounds add noise and misrepresent the project's supported browsers; shared templates should reflect current browser support.
common_pattern: Removing legacy/redundant markup from shared HTML templates so they reflect modern HTML5 defaults and the project's actual browser-support requirements.

text: Do not hard-code `fill` (or other presentational colour) attributes inside SVG sprite `<symbol>` markup; define fill colours in Sass/SCSS and apply them via CSS selectors.
reason: Hard-coded fills can't be themed or overridden via CSS; centralizing colour in Sass keeps presentation in the stylesheet layer and lets sprites inherit theme colours.
common_pattern: Conventions for the project's SVG icon system: centralized sprite library (`svg_sprites.html`) plus a single rendering entry point (`patterns/components/icon/icon.html`), with rules covering how to render icons, when to add to the sprite, keeping the global sprite lean, avoiding duplicates, and keeping presentational styling out of SVG markup.

text: Use `aria-expanded` (and `aria-controls`) only on toggle buttons that control expandable regions, updating `aria-expanded` when the region opens/closes. For non-expandable components (e.g., alerts), do not set `aria-expanded`; control visual state via dedicated state classes instead.
reason: ARIA state attributes must match the element's semantic role to provide accurate information to assistive technologies. Applying `aria-expanded` to non-expandable widgets is misleading, while omitting it on actual toggles removes useful state cues.
common_pattern: ARIA state attributes (specifically aria-expanded) should be applied only to elements whose semantic role supports expanded/collapsed states; other state changes use CSS classes instead.

text: In HTML templates, format tags with exactly one space between attributes and no space before the closing `>` (e.g., `<tag attr1 attr2>`, not `<tag attr1 attr2 >` or `<tag attr1attr2>`).
reason: Ensures valid, consistent markup and prevents browsers from mis-parsing attributes (e.g., breaking accessibility attributes).
common_pattern: Correct whitespace formatting within HTML tags in templates: exactly one space between attributes, and no extraneous space before the closing angle bracket.

text: In Wagtail templates, use CMS-provided page fields and official Wagtail template tags (e.g., `{{ page.title }}`, `{% wagtail_site %}`, and page fields such as `page.social_text`/`page.listing_intro`) rather than hardcoded content or ad-hoc request-based lookups.
reason: Keeps rendered content editable through the CMS, prevents drift between templates and page data, follows Wagtail conventions, and ensures site context and SEO metadata are populated correctly.
common_pattern: Wagtail templates should use CMS-provided page fields and official Wagtail template tags instead of hardcoded content or ad-hoc request lookups.

text: In styleguide pattern YAML fixtures (e.g., `project_styleguide`), use fictional placeholder names — generic or pun-based — instead of real individuals' names, even when the design mockups show a real name.
reason: Avoids implying endorsement and prevents privacy/branding issues from embedding real identities in demo content.
common_pattern: Placeholder identity values in styleguide/demo fixtures must be fictional (generic or pun names), never real individuals' names.

text: Use `align-items: flex-start` when aligning flex children to the start of the cross axis; do not use `flex-basis: start` for that purpose, because `flex-basis` expects main-axis sizing values such as lengths, percentages, `auto`, or `content`.
reason: `flex-basis: start` is not a valid flex-basis value. Using the correct property/value makes the intended alignment explicit and keeps the CSS valid.
common_pattern: CSS flexbox best practices for layout, sizing, and alignment in the Wagtailio codebase.

text: Write CSS/SCSS shorthand values (padding, margin, etc.) in their shortest valid form: collapse redundant trailing values (e.g. `padding: 15px 0 0` instead of `padding: 15px 0 0 0`), omit units on zero (e.g. `0` not `0px`), and separate values with single spaces (no accidental double spaces).
reason: Reduces redundancy, matches the project's existing concise shorthand style, keeps declarations readable, and avoids noisy diffs.
common_pattern: CSS/SCSS shorthand property values should be written in their most concise, idiomatic form: omit redundant trailing values, drop units on zero, and use clean single-space separation.

text: In Wagtail templates, render images with the `{% image %}` template tag (e.g. `{% image item.image width-400 class="..." alt=item.image.alt %}`) rather than hand-writing ``, so renditions and inherited attributes such as alt text are applied automatically.
reason: The `{% image %}` tag inherits alt text and other attributes from the Wagtail image model and generates correct renditions; a raw `` tag bypasses this and forces manual/duplicated attribute handling.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns govern how images are handled in this Wagtail project: use Wagtail's native rendering facilities rather than hand-rolled `` markup, and prefer WebP-optimized image assets to reduce payload. The unifying theme is 'let the framework/format do image handling correctly and efficiently', but the two halves address distinct mechanisms (template tag rendering vs. asset format/optimization).

text: Serve static image assets (e.g. under `static/img/`) as WebP, compressed with an image optimizer (Squoosh CLI/Web UI) before committing, when it substantially reduces file size and no PNG-specific feature is required; for tiny icon renditions (e.g. `max-100x100`) treat WebP conversion as an optional optimization, and add `format-webp` to Wagtail `{% image %}` tags when byte savings are worthwhile.
reason: WebP provides superior compression without noticeable quality loss, drastically reducing payload (e.g. 1.1MB → 170KB) and improving page load performance; for tiny icons the savings are negligible and may not justify the extra filter.
scope: project-wide for static image assets and Wagtail image tags
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns govern how images are handled in this Wagtail project: use Wagtail's native rendering facilities rather than hand-rolled `` markup, and prefer WebP-optimized image assets to reduce payload. The unifying theme is 'let the framework/format do image handling correctly and efficiently', but the two halves address distinct mechanisms (template tag rendering vs. asset format/optimization).

text: In wagtailio component SCSS (`wagtailio/static/sass/components/*.scss`), set every grid child's `grid-column: <start> / span <n>` so the span equals the number of content columns actually available in `_grid.scss` at the active breakpoint (e.g. `span 2` on the 2-column mobile grid, `span 5` at large), and adjust the span per breakpoint using `@include media-query(...)`. Do not reuse a larger span across elements or breakpoints, and never span more columns than the grid defines at that breakpoint.
reason: Matches the project's responsive column grid, prevents overflows/implicit columns at narrow breakpoints and under-filled rows at wide ones, and keeps text-heavy elements from colliding with adjacent columns (e.g. decorative icons).
common_pattern: Responsive CSS Grid column spans in wagtailio component SCSS must be derived from the shared grid's actual content-column count at each breakpoint, tuned per breakpoint via the project's media-query mixin rather than reusing a single span value.

text: For repeated item/card grids in component SCSS, make items equal height across rows using CSS Grid capabilities where possible; fall back to a `min-height` on the items only when Grid cannot achieve the desired equal-height behavior.
reason: Equal-height items produce a more consistent, tidy layout across repeated rows.
common_pattern: Responsive CSS Grid column spans in wagtailio component SCSS must be derived from the shared grid's actual content-column count at each breakpoint, tuned per breakpoint via the project's media-query mixin rather than reusing a single span value.

text: In JS component classes, when a class name is stored as an instance property (e.g. `this.activeClass = 'active'`), reference that property in all `classList` checks and mutations instead of repeating the literal string.
reason: Distinct sub-pattern about centralizing the class-name constant in JS; supported by one PR but a clear, non-overlapping rule.
common_pattern: Styling and class-naming conventions in Sass/templates that favor explicit, self-contained, component-owned class names over implicit coupling (parent overrides, structural selectors, value-based names), plus related upkeep rules for JS class-name constants and CSS selectors when markup changes.

text: When two conditions are guaranteed mutually exclusive (exactly one must hold), express that exclusivity directly in the branching instead of writing two independent `if` statements. When consuming an already-validated invariant, use `if`/`else` (or `elif`) rather than re-checking the complementary condition with a second `if`. When performing the validation, collapse the two invalid states (both set / neither set) into a single combined check such as `operator.xor(bool(a), bool(b))` or `bool(a) is bool(b)` rather than separate `if not a and not b` and `if a and b` branches.
reason: Mirrors the invariant enforced by validation, signals to readers that the branches cannot both execute, avoids redundant defensive re-checks that duplicate the validation's contract, and keeps the coupled conditions visibly in sync.
common_pattern: Encoding a known mutual-exclusivity invariant (exactly one of two conditions holds) explicitly in the code structure rather than as two independent `if` statements — both when consuming an already-validated invariant and when performing the validation itself.

text: Style icons consistently: use the same sizing scale as equivalent icons in other components, and when rendering repeated icon sets, apply the same transforms/orientation to every icon unless the variation is an intentional design choice.
reason: Maintains visual consistency across the UI and prevents ad-hoc sizing or transform variations that look like styling bugs.
scope: Component styles (e.g., `wagtailio/static/sass/components/`) and repeated icon sets
common_pattern: Icon styling should be visually consistent: equivalent icons should share the same sizing scale, and repeated icon sets should share the same transforms/orientation unless a variation is intentional.

text: Use `pointer-events: none` on decorative icons or overlays nested inside interactive controls (e.g., modal close buttons) so pointer events pass through to the parent control, but do not add it to elements hidden via `display: none`, where it is redundant.
reason: Prevents decorative layers from intercepting clicks intended for the interactive parent, while avoiding redundant CSS declarations on elements that cannot receive pointer events anyway.
common_pattern: Guidance on when to apply `pointer-events: none`: apply it to decorative icons nested inside interactive controls so clicks reach the parent, but do not apply it to elements hidden with `display: none` because it is redundant.

text: In SCSS/Sass, define color variables using hex notation rather than rgb()/rgba() functional notation; for semi-transparent colors, use 8-digit hex values that include the alpha channel (e.g. #2626264d).
reason: Maintains consistency with existing _variables.scss conventions and makes color values easier to scan and reuse.
common_pattern: Both generalizations require SCSS/Sass color variables to use hex notation instead of rgb()/rgba() notation, including 8-digit hex values when an alpha channel is needed.

text: In Django/Wagtail templates, avoid repeated or per-item queryset evaluation: prepare querysets at the view/queryset level (e.g., call `PageQuerySet.specific()` before rendering), use `.exists()` for boolean checks, bind repeated filter/queryset expressions with `{% with %}`, and do not call queryset methods such as `.all` on StreamField/ListBlock values—iterate those list-like values directly with `{% for item in value.items %}`.
reason: Prevents N+1/database-query overhead and incorrect template API usage, keeping template rendering efficient and correct.
common_pattern: Optimizing Django/Wagtail template data access: avoid repeated or per-item queryset evaluation and use correct template syntax for list-like block values.

text: When a component contains absolutely positioned children, set `position: relative` on the component's root selector to establish the containing block for those children.
reason: Without an explicit positioned ancestor, absolute children resolve against a farther ancestor or the viewport, causing unexpected offsets and layout that is harder to reason about.
scope: CSS/Sass component styling, especially BEM component root classes
common_pattern: CSS positioning conventions for component styles: prefer the modern `inset` shorthand for offsets and ensure absolutely positioned children are positioned relative to their intended containing element.

text: When overriding a template block to augment inherited content, include `{{ block.super }}` to preserve the parent's output. Do not declare empty block overrides that contain no content.
reason: Prevents accidental loss of parent block content, keeps template overrides additive, and avoids unnecessary lines and maintenance cost.
common_pattern: Best practices for Django template inheritance: extending the appropriate base template, avoiding duplication, preserving parent blocks with block.super, and documenting intentional deviations.

text: Mark table header cells — including header cells that contain images/logos rather than text — as `<th>`, reserving `<td>` for data cells. When table markup is produced by a generator (e.g. a StreamField table), that generator must support emitting `<th>` header rows so generated output stays semantically consistent with the pattern-library template.
reason: Semantic `<th>` markup associates headers with their data cells, which screen readers rely on and which yields correct default styling/behavior. If the generator cannot emit headers, the rendered table silently diverges from the semantic structure the templates assume.
common_pattern: Semantic table markup: header cells (including image/logo cells) must be `<th>`, never `<td>`, and any markup generator (e.g. StreamField table) must be able to emit these semantic headers rather than relying on hardcoded header markup in pattern-library-only templates.

text: In `_comparison-table.scss`, size the first column (`td:first-child`) with explicit `width` at breakpoints — `width: 250px` at the large breakpoint and `width: 150px` at the small breakpoint — instead of relying on `min-width: fit-content`, which has no reliable effect when header image sizes vary.
reason: Explicit per-breakpoint widths give predictable, intentional column sizing; `min-width: fit-content` either had no effect or depended on variable header images, producing unstable table alignment.
common_pattern: Responsive table column sizing in SCSS should use explicit `width` values at defined breakpoints instead of `min-width: fit-content`, because `fit-content` is unreliable (no effect or varies with content like header images). One generalization about page-level `overflow-x` scrolling is an outlier with a different concern.

text: For responsive table components, localize horizontal scrolling to the table container/body with `overflow-x` gated by `@include media-query(...)` breakpoints, rather than letting the whole page scroll horizontally.
reason: Keeps horizontal scrolling scoped to wide table content and improves usability on narrow viewports.
common_pattern: Responsive table column sizing in SCSS should use explicit `width` values at defined breakpoints instead of `min-width: fit-content`, because `fit-content` is unreliable (no effect or varies with content like header images). One generalization about page-level `overflow-x` scrolling is an outlier with a different concern.

text: Frontend templates should render only user-facing content; structural or editor-facing values (e.g., heading/label fields that exist for CMS structure) should be omitted from markup rather than output to the page.
reason: Rendering backend/structural metadata on the frontend surfaces values that were never meant for end users and adds unnecessary markup.
common_pattern: Frontend templates must render semantically correct content: fields should be named for what they actually represent, and templates should only output user-facing content (not structural/CMS-only values).

text: When compiling a class's inheritance list, order mixins before concrete base classes and omit any base class that one of the mixins already inherits (e.g. if a mixin derives from StructBlock, do not also list StructBlock).
reason: Keeps the MRO unambiguous and intentional: mixins placed first can override/augment base behavior, and re-listing a base already provided by a mixin is redundant inheritance that only clutters the MRO.
common_pattern: Python mixin/inheritance design: structuring class base lists for a clean MRO and centralizing shared configuration (value_class) on the mixin so subclasses inherit it exactly once.

text: When a value class (e.g. a StructValue subclass) is shared by multiple block models through a mixin, define the value class above the mixin, assign it as the mixin's value_class, and let consuming block classes inherit that assignment rather than redeclaring it.
reason: Python evaluates class bodies top-to-bottom, so the referenced class must be defined first; centralizing the assignment on the mixin eliminates per-block duplication and keeps every consumer on the same StructValue behavior.
common_pattern: Python mixin/inheritance design: structuring class base lists for a clean MRO and centralizing shared configuration (value_class) on the mixin so subclasses inherit it exactly once.

text: When a flex-wrapped list does not fill its container (leaving unbalanced trailing whitespace on one side), center the items with `justify-content: center` instead of letting them align to the start — apply this in the mobile/default styles when the imbalance appears on small viewports.
reason: Prevents visually awkward unbalanced whitespace when wrapped flex rows are narrower than their container.
common_pattern: Flex-wrapped lists/rows that don't fill their container leave unbalanced trailing whitespace on one side; the fix is to center the flex items with `justify-content: center` instead of the default start alignment.

text: Do not flag featured/curated posts inline inside the main chronological listing loop via a membership test like `post in featured_posts`. Render the featured subset as its own section or derive it explicitly; if the design requires featured items interspersed every N posts, implement explicit spacing/interleaving logic rather than relying on collection membership.
reason: Inline membership tests conflate 'latest posts' with 'featured posts', causing all overlapping recent posts to render as featured and producing unpredictable counts/order; explicit separation keeps latest vs. curated concerns controlled.
common_pattern: Separate featured/curated posts from the main chronological listing loop instead of marking them inline by membership in a featured set; derive or render the special subset explicitly, and use explicit interleaving only when the design requires it.

text: Mark elements that are purely decorative (inline SVG icons, icons inside a control that already has an accessible name) with aria-hidden="true" so screen readers ignore them, unless the icon itself conveys meaning.
reason: Decorative icons do not carry meaning beyond adjacent text or a parent control's label; announcing them creates redundant or confusing screen-reader noise.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct ARIA / accessible-name usage in HTML templates: how to name landmarks and interactive elements, when to hide decorative content from assistive tech, and when to avoid redundant ARIA. The cluster is coherent as 'accessibility-in-templates' but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns.

text: Give each landmark region (<nav>, <header>, <main>, <section>) a distinct, context-accurate accessible name placed on the landmark element itself (not on inner elements like <ul>), preferring aria-labelledby that references an existing translatable heading over a literal aria-label.
reason: Assistive-tech users navigate by landmarks; unique labels let them distinguish regions, labeling the wrong element produces no landmark announcement, and aria-labelledby keeps the name translatable by i18n frameworks.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct ARIA / accessible-name usage in HTML templates: how to name landmarks and interactive elements, when to hide decorative content from assistive tech, and when to avoid redundant ARIA. The cluster is coherent as 'accessibility-in-templates' but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns.

text: Use a single source for an element's accessible name: do not override a visible label with aria-label or add redundant u-sr-only text next to an aria-label, and for image/icon-only links or buttons provide an explicit accessible name (e.g. aria-label from the item's human-readable name). When repeated links share identical visible text, disambiguate them with aria-describedby pointing to a per-item element that carries a unique generated id.
reason: aria-label overrides visible text and hidden spans, so duplicate naming sources create dead markup and mismatch between what sighted assistive-tech users see and what is announced; image-only and repeated-text controls otherwise have ambiguous or empty accessible names.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct ARIA / accessible-name usage in HTML templates: how to name landmarks and interactive elements, when to hide decorative content from assistive tech, and when to avoid redundant ARIA. The cluster is coherent as 'accessibility-in-templates' but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns.

text: Rely on native HTML semantics: do not add a role that duplicates an element's implicit/default ARIA role, and avoid aria-roledescription unless it solves a specific, documented accessibility problem.
reason: Native elements already expose their default roles; redundant roles and advanced ARIA add noise and risk conflicts or misuse.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern correct ARIA / accessible-name usage in HTML templates: how to name landmarks and interactive elements, when to hide decorative content from assistive tech, and when to avoid redundant ARIA. The cluster is coherent as 'accessibility-in-templates' but contains several genuinely distinct sub-patterns.

text: For Wagtail admin menu groups and viewsets, choose labels and icons that are semantically appropriate and distinct from core UI landmarks. Use singular, non-pluralized labels for model groups (e.g. "Taxonomy", not "Taxonomies"), and choose non-page icons that reflect the model's function (e.g. "form" or "tasks") rather than reusing Page/Page-button icons such as "doc-full-inverse" or "folder-open-inverse".
reason: Consistent, semantically accurate admin labels and icons make the Wagtail admin UI easier to scan and prevent unrelated model landmarks from being confused with page-related controls.
common_pattern: Wagtail admin menu UI configuration should use semantically meaningful labels and icons that reflect the entity's purpose and avoid confusion with core page/UI landmarks.

text: When building a list from an iterable via a one-to-one mapping (e.g., each item to a dict), prefer `list.extend(generator_expression)` over a manual `for` loop with `append()` as the idiomatic default — but keep the explicit loop when local benchmarks show `append()` is measurably faster in the hot path (e.g., template tags).
reason: `extend` with a generator is more concise and idiomatic while preserving lazy one-to-one transformation; however, benchmarking can reveal that `append()` is marginally faster, in which case readability gains are outweighed by an unnecessary performance regression.
common_pattern: Idiomatic vs. performance trade-off when building a list from an iterable in Python (extend with a generator vs. explicit for-loop with append)

text: In a model's save() hook, prefer unconditional cache invalidation over an existence-check-then-delete pattern, since a cache delete is cheaper than the extra DB query. Exception: when the model represents multiple navigation versions/configurations, only invalidate when the saved instance is the active/used one (e.g., referenced by a settings relation), to avoid purging unrelated versions.
reason: Unconditional clearing avoids a DB query per save and stays correct, but in models with multiple coexisting configurations it causes unnecessary cache churn, so a targeted check is warranted only in that case.
common_pattern: Cache invalidation strategy in a model's save() hook: the trade-off between unconditional cache deletion (avoids an extra DB query) and conditional invalidation (avoids invalidating unrelated configurations/versions).

text: For content that must remain accessible while visually hidden — such as form labels — add descriptive text and apply the project's screen-reader-only utility class (`u-sr-only`) instead of hiding it with `display: none`. Remove any component SCSS rules that hide the same element with `display: none`.
reason: `display: none` removes the element from the accessibility tree, so screen readers cannot announce it. Using the shared visually-hidden utility keeps the content available to assistive technology and centralizes hiding behavior instead of scattering conflicting component CSS.
common_pattern: Accessible visually-hidden content should use the project's screen-reader-only utility class instead of `display: none`, and any component CSS that hides the same element must be removed to avoid conflicting or redundant hiding behavior.

text: Match the prevailing indentation style of the existing file/codebase for new or changed lines, and if `.editorconfig` conflicts with that style, update `.editorconfig` to match the codebase instead of reformatting existing files.
reason: This keeps diffs focused on functional changes, avoids whitespace-only churn, and prevents tooling or editor configuration from fighting the established code style.
common_pattern: Maintain the existing indentation conventions of the file/codebase; do not introduce formatting churn, and resolve `.editorconfig` conflicts by aligning config to the existing codebase rather than reformatting files.

text: When a component variant, hover/state, or decorative-icon overlay changes an element's background, explicitly set a contrasting text/icon `color` (from the existing project `$color--*` tokens) in that selector rather than relying on inherited/default colors, and verify the text/background pairing passes contrast checks.
reason: Variants and states can pair an inherited text color with a non-contrasting background (or vice versa), making text unreadable; repeated/re-declared color properties in state selectors prevent icons or labels from disappearing against light or forced-color backgrounds.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern CSS/Sass accessibility: ensuring color contrast for text/graphics across default, variant/state, and forced-colors (WHCM) rendering modes, including correct use of forced-colors media queries and system color keywords.

text:
Use heading elements only for real document-outline headings and keep the hierarchy sequential: render the page's primary heading as an `

` (not a generic `
`), section headings immediately below it as `

`/`

` without skipping levels, and mark up purely visual subheadings (e.g. `hero__subheading`) as a `

` with the styling class rather than a heading element. When a heading's level changes, update its descendant headings to the immediately following level.
reason: Skipped or decorative headings produce an incorrect, noisy document outline that confuses assistive technology and hurts accessibility and SEO; sequential, semantic headings preserve a correct outline for screen-reader navigation.
common_pattern: Correct semantic use of HTML heading elements so the document outline/heading hierarchy stays accurate for accessibility (and SEO): headings only where they belong, no skipped levels; plus handling the CSS side-effects of changing an element's semantic type.

text: In Django templates, close blocks with an explicit block name, e.g. `{% endblock block_name %}`, rather than a bare `{% endblock %}`, especially in base templates that are inherited by larger templates.
reason: Explicit block names make the closing tag self-documenting in large or inherited templates, improving readability and review.
scope: Django templates, especially base templates with inheritance
common_pattern: Consistent formatting and structural clarity in Django/Wagtail HTML templates: spacing inside template delimiters, indentation/nesting of template tags and HTML elements, and explicit block closure.

text: New HTML/Django templates should be formatted with `djhtml` (or the project's configured template formatter) before committing.
reason: Consistent template formatting reduces diff noise and ensures new files match project conventions.
common_pattern: New HTML/Django templates should be formatted with the project's template formatter (`djhtml`) before committing to keep formatting consistent and reduce diff noise.

text: In CSS reset/normalization, only target elements that actually have browser-default styling to reset, and verify the selector matches the rendered element and is not overridden by more specific or later-loaded rules (check specificity and stylesheet import order).
reason: Prevents redundant resets on elements without default styles and avoids silently ineffective resets such as `list-style: none` failing due to selector mismatch or rule precedence.
common_pattern: CSS reset/normalization rules should precisely target elements that actually have browser-default styling, and reset selectors must be verified to match the rendered element and not be overridden by specificity or stylesheet load order.

text: Use existing CSS classes for text styling instead of hardcoding font-size values or relying on redundant presentational HTML tags (e.g., <b>) when a class already applies the styling.
reason: Keeps typography consistent, centralized, and avoids duplicated or redundant style declarations.
common_pattern: Styling responsibility should be centralized in CSS classes rather than hardcoded in component SCSS or applied via redundant presentational HTML tags.

text: For form/component layouts with adjacent body text and a decorative icon or illustration that may overlap at some viewports, wrap each in its own container and use `display: flex` so each element responds to its container. Avoid CSS offsets such as `inset` or absolute positioning for the icon. On mobile viewports, stack the icon below the text using `flex-direction: column` within the relevant `@include media-query(...)` breakpoint.
reason: Prevents text/icon overlap and unreadable text at intermediate viewports, and avoids brittle offset-based positioning that is difficult to maintain responsively.
common_pattern: Use flexbox for adjacent text and decorative icon/illustration to prevent overlap, with responsive stacking on mobile, avoiding absolute positioning or offset properties like `inset`.

text: For large repeating background patterns, use a small square tile (e.g., 60px) instead of a full-size image, and render it with CSS tiling (`background-size` set to the tile's dimensions and `background-repeat: repeat`) to cut asset size while preserving the visual result. Apply this in the relevant `::before` rules (e.g., `.template-wagtail-space-index-page, .template-wagtail-space-page`).
reason: Drastically reduces asset file size (e.g., ~1.7MB to ~7KB) while maintaining the same visual appearance through seamless CSS tiling.
common_pattern: Optimizing large repeating background images by replacing them with small square tiles rendered via CSS `background-size`/`background-repeat` tiling.

text: In newsletter templates rendered in both email and web contexts, use the existing rendering-context flag (e.g., email/web or page.preview) to conditionally render email-only elements—such as unsubscribe/update-preference links, ESP merge tags, and 'view this email online' links—so they are omitted from the web version. Apply the same condition to every occurrence rather than duplicating the template or fixing only one instance.
reason: Email-only placeholders do not resolve outside the ESP, and email-specific links are redundant or confusing on the web page. Conditional rendering keeps a single template maintainable while preventing dead links and inconsistent output.
scope: newsletter/MJML templates shared between email and web
common_pattern: Conditional rendering of email-only elements in newsletter templates shared between email and web contexts.

text: In Django templates, reference compiled frontend assets (JS/CSS bundles) with the project's `{% manifest 'path' %}` tag instead of `{% static 'path' %}`, and ensure `manifest` is included in the template's `{% load %}` line.
reason: Resolves asset URLs through the manifest loader so templates point at the hashed filenames produced by the build pipeline, preventing stale or broken asset links after deployments.
common_pattern: Use a manifest loader for compiled frontend assets in Django templates instead of direct {% static %} paths, with supporting Webpack/Django configuration for hashed filenames.

text: Place code in the module that matches its scope and domain: feature/domain-specific code (models, page types, blocks, templates) belongs in the dedicated feature app/module rather than in shared/generic modules like `core` or `navigation`, while genuinely cross-cutting shared definitions (enums, choices, shared types) belong in the core/domain module; keep narrowly-scoped utility snippets in the utility module. Avoid catch-all `utils/` packages and avoid relocating unrelated code into a content/domain module, so shared modules hold only truly cross-cutting code.
reason: Aligning module placement with code scope keeps each app cohesive around its own domain and shared packages free of feature-specific code, making ownership/discovery predictable, keeping shared domain definitions discoverable, and allowing features to be cleanly untangled or removed later without misleading relocations or review churn.
common_pattern: Feature/domain-specific code (models, blocks, templates) belongs in the app dedicated to that feature, not in shared/generic modules like `core` or `navigation`.

text: Do not suppress Stylelint violations with inline `/* stylelint-disable-line ... */` comments; instead fix the code by using the project's preferred equivalent (e.g., the `inset` shorthand instead of physical `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`) or update the Stylelint config — removing the property from `property-disallowed-list` when it is genuinely used across the codebase.
reason: Inline disables hide the underlying issue and fragment the linting policy; fixing the code or the config keeps linting meaningful and consistent across the codebase.
common_pattern: Stylelint configuration should remain aligned with the project's canonical preset and reflect actual project usage, rather than carrying stale preset references, unused-framework ignore rules, or inline rule suppressions.

text: In Sass/CSS, use the `inset` shorthand instead of separate `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left` declarations when setting positioning offsets.
reason: `inset` is more concise, modern, reduces repetition, and keeps related offset values together.
common_pattern: CSS positioning conventions for component styles: prefer the modern `inset` shorthand for offsets and ensure absolutely positioned children are positioned relative to their intended containing element.

text: In Wagtail page model classes, declare the page-hierarchy attributes (`parent_page_types`, `subpage_types`) first in the class body before `template`, fields, and panels, and add an inline comment explaining the intent of any non-obvious class-level constraint (e.g. `max_count`, restricted `parent_page_types`) so future developers don't silently remove it.
reason: Putting hierarchy declarations first makes a page's structural role scannable at a glance, and commenting constraints (which encode product decisions not evident from the code) prevents accidental removal or misunderstanding.
common_pattern: Wagtail-specific authoring conventions for page models and block fields (class-body organization, documented constraints, generic field/message naming, correct block arguments, and accurate docs).

text: Place app-specific Django/Wagtail template tags in that app's `templatetags/` directory rather than in a shared or unrelated app's templatetags module.
reason: Keeps app-specific template-tag code co-located with the app, improving discoverability, modularity, and avoiding bloating shared templatetags modules.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns govern correct organization and use of Django/Wagtail custom template tag libraries: `{% load %}` declarations should match actual usage, and app-specific tag libraries should live in the owning app's `templatetags/` directory.

text: In flex components, add `flex-shrink: 0` to SVG/icon descendants that must retain their intrinsic size when adjacent text content grows or wraps.
reason: Prevents icons from being compressed by long flex siblings, preserving intended component layout and icon dimensions.
common_pattern: CSS flexbox best practices for layout, sizing, and alignment in the Wagtailio codebase.

text: In component styles, use one flex declaration style per element: do not separately declare `flex-grow`, `flex-shrink`, or `flex-basis` when a `flex` shorthand on the same selector already sets those values.
reason: The `flex` shorthand already defines flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis, so separate longhand declarations are redundant and can make it unclear which value is intended.
common_pattern: CSS flexbox best practices for layout, sizing, and alignment in the Wagtailio codebase.

text: In templates, consolidate duplicated or near-identical conditional branches into a single block: resolve the differing value before the check (e.g. `{% firstof primary fallback as resolved_value %}`) and guard once, rather than repeating the same condition or include across multiple branches.
reason: Eliminates redundant conditions that drift out of sync and keeps shared parameters in one place.
common_pattern: Refactoring template conditional logic: consolidating duplicated/over-complex branch conditions and simplifying them by moving resolution into a single normalized context flag or model property, so a template condition reads one source of truth.

text: In SCSS/CSS (including `wagtailio/static/sass/` component and base files such as `base/_typography.scss`), use `rem` units instead of `px` for sizing, spacing, font-size, and icon dimensions so styles scale with the user's root font size and browser accessibility settings. When converting Figma `px` values to `rem`, use the project's 16px base (`design_px / 16`) and choose exact whole-pixel equivalents (e.g. 34px → 2.125rem, not 2.138rem) so rendered font-sizes and line-heights match the design source.
reason: `rem` units respect user font-size/zoom preferences and browser accessibility settings, keeping layouts and icons proportional and consistent with the project's stylesheet conventions. Figma is the design source of truth; imprecise rem values silently produce wrong rendered sizes and break visual fidelity, while whole-pixel equivalents are easier to reason about.
common_pattern: SCSS/CSS unit conventions: prefer `rem` over `px` for sizing/spacing/typography, and when translating Figma design px values to rem, use exact whole-pixel conversions that match the design source.

text: When changing a component's root element for semantic/accessibility reasons (e.g., replacing a non-semantic `<div>` with a semantic heading such as `<h1>`), update its CSS selectors and associated styles to match the new element, including resetting or overriding browser-default margins via the component's modifier class to preserve the intended layout.
reason: Changing element types requires keeping component styles in sync and preventing layout shifts from browser-default spacing such as heading margins.
common_pattern: Correct semantic use of HTML heading elements so the document outline/heading hierarchy stays accurate for accessibility (and SEO): headings only where they belong, no skipped levels; plus handling the CSS side-effects of changing an element's semantic type.

text: Use Django template comments `{# ... #}` for developer notes instead of HTML comments `<!-- -->`, since HTML comments are emitted into the rendered output.
reason: Distinct syntax-level rule from PR #546: HTML comments pollute the client output while template comments are stripped at render time.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern the content and syntax of comments in (Django) templates: comments should earn their place by adding non-obvious, audience-appropriate context rather than restating code, and should use template comment syntax that is stripped from output.

text: In SCSS/CSS files, follow the project's whitespace and blank-line conventions consistently: include a space between selectors and opening braces (`.foo {`), no whitespace before semicolons, no blank lines inside rule blocks, and a single trailing newline. However, separate nested at-rule blocks such as `@include media-query(...)` from preceding declarations (and from preceding media-query blocks) with a blank line. Indent closing braces and nested declarations to match their opening level so nesting depth is clear.
reason: Uniform stylesheet formatting improves readability, makes selector nesting obvious, prevents mis-nesting, avoids noisy diffs and linter/formatter churn, and visually distinguishes base declarations from responsive overrides so the responsive structure is easier to scan.
common_pattern: SCSS/CSS stylesheet formatting and organization conventions: whitespace/spacing hygiene, indentation, blank-line grouping of media-query blocks, and avoiding redundant responsive overrides.

text: In Wagtail/Django templates, align `{% if %}` conditionals with the model field's requiredness: wrap optional fields (nullable / `blank=True`, may be `None` or blank) in `{% if field %}` before rendering their markup so no empty elements are emitted and the literal `None` is never shown. Do NOT wrap fields that are required in the model (`blank=False`) — instead enforce requiredness at the model/validation layer and keep the UI rendering consistent with that contract. Also skip adding guard conditionals when an existing `{% for %}` loop already outputs nothing for empty/`None` values.
reason: Prevents a class of template bugs (empty headings, empty `<a>` tags, literal 'None' output) while avoiding dead conditional branches for fields guaranteed to be present. Keeps the source of truth for presence in `models.py`.
common_pattern: Template conditionals should mirror model field requiredness: guard optional (nullable/blank) fields with `{% if %}` before emitting markup, and never guard required fields — enforce requiredness at the model layer instead. Redundant guards (e.g. when a loop already handles absence) should also be avoided.

text: Render icons in templates by including the shared icon component (`patterns/components/icon/icon.html`) with the `icon` name (and optional `classes`/`variant`) rather than writing inline `<svg>` markup. Before adding a new icon, check `patterns/includes/svg_sprites.html` for an existing suitable icon and use it; add a new `<symbol>` only when the icon is genuinely new or visually distinct. Maintain one canonical `<symbol>` per icon in `svg_sprites.html`, removing duplicates and keeping the variant compatible with the `icon.html` template.
reason: Centralizes icon markup/definitions, keeps templates consistent with the design system, avoids duplicated SVG, and makes icon updates apply project-wide. Reusing existing sprite icons prevents redundant one-off SVGs, and a single canonical symbol per icon avoids duplicate symbols while guaranteeing correct rendering through the shared icon template.
common_pattern: Conventions for the project's SVG icon system: centralized sprite library (`svg_sprites.html`) plus a single rendering entry point (`patterns/components/icon/icon.html`), with rules covering how to render icons, when to add to the sprite, keeping the global sprite lean, avoiding duplicates, and keeping presentational styling out of SVG markup.

text: Keep the globally rendered `patterns/includes/svg_sprites.html` reserved for icons used across the site; icons used on only a single page or section belong in an external SVG file or a page/section-specific template, not the shared sprite.
reason: The global sprite is rendered as a Django template on every page, so page-specific SVGs inflate every page's response size and render cost.
common_pattern: Conventions for the project's SVG icon system: centralized sprite library (`svg_sprites.html`) plus a single rendering entry point (`patterns/components/icon/icon.html`), with rules covering how to render icons, when to add to the sprite, keeping the global sprite lean, avoiding duplicates, and keeping presentational styling out of SVG markup.

text: In base templates, place the SVG sprite include (`includes/svg_sprites.html`) in the `<head>` or near the top of the document so symbols are defined before page content references them.
reason: Ensures SVG symbols are available before markup uses them, preventing missing/broken icons and ordering-related rendering issues.
common_pattern: Conventions for the project's SVG icon system: centralized sprite library (`svg_sprites.html`) plus a single rendering entry point (`patterns/components/icon/icon.html`), with rules covering how to render icons, when to add to the sprite, keeping the global sprite lean, avoiding duplicates, and keeping presentational styling out of SVG markup.

text: Do not embed inline `<script>` blocks in templates. Place page-specific JavaScript in a dedicated static JS file and load it from the template that needs it, so the project can enforce a Content Security Policy that disallows inline JavaScript.
reason: A future CSP will block inline JS; external scripts loaded via `<script src=...>` can be allowed by CSP while keeping templates clean.
common_pattern: Django template script organization — controlling where JavaScript lives in templates: keeping global scripts outside child-overridable blocks, keeping page-specific scripts out of shared base templates, and extracting inline JS into static files.

text: When creating a page template, extend the most specific existing template that already provides the needed shared structure and override only the blocks that differ, rather than duplicating shared blocks. If you intentionally duplicate another template's behavior, add a comment explaining why.
reason: Avoids duplication of meta tags, body classes, and other shared blocks, keeps a single source of truth so changes propagate, and makes intentional deviations clear to future maintainers.
scope: project templates using Django/Wagtail template inheritance, especially page templates
common_pattern: Best practices for Django template inheritance: extending the appropriate base template, avoiding duplication, preserving parent blocks with block.super, and documenting intentional deviations.

text: Declare explicit pixel dimensions on icon elements: use the exact design-spec size (e.g., 34x34px, equal width and height) for styled icons, and give favicon link elements an explicit pixel `sizes` value (e.g., `sizes="32x32"`) rather than `sizes="any"`.
reason: Exact dimensions prevent visual drift from the design spec and avoid browser bugs (e.g., Chrome preferring an ICO over an SVG favicon when `sizes="any"` is used).
common_pattern: Icon and favicon elements should declare explicit, exact pixel dimensions rather than relying on approximate values, defaults, or vague size tokens.

text: Interactive icons must have a minimum 24x24px clickable/tap target, achieved via padding or `min-width`/`min-height` around the glyph when the icon itself is smaller.
reason: Small hit areas (e.g., 16x16) are hard to click and hurt accessibility, especially when surrounding elements don't signal clickability.
common_pattern: Icon and favicon elements should declare explicit, exact pixel dimensions rather than relying on approximate values, defaults, or vague size tokens.

text: Do not add `target="_blank"` (or otherwise force new tabs/windows) to external links in templates; let the browser and the user's preferences decide link behavior. If a link does open in a new tab (`target="_blank"`), include visually hidden text such as `(opens in a new tab)` so screen reader users are warned of the browsing-context change.
reason: Forcing new tabs overrides user preference and accessibility settings and is the project-wide template convention. When a new tab is nonetheless used, screen reader users must be warned of the browsing-context change via visually hidden text.
scope: project-wide template convention; global new-tab accessibility fallback
common_pattern: Project convention governing `target="_blank"` on external links: whether to force new tabs (resolved to 'no' by the Wagtail-issue rationale) plus the accessibility requirement triggered when a new-tab link is used anyway.

text: Always provide a clearly visible focus indicator for interactive elements; never remove the default focus outline (e.g., `outline: none`) without supplying a custom, high-contrast replacement. Hover/focus states should be MORE visible than the base state (e.g., stronger color, underline, sufficient contrast against dark backgrounds) rather than LESS visible (e.g., reduced opacity). For interactive elements in Sass components, pair `&:hover` with `&:focus-visible` rather than `&:focus` when styling focus states.
reason: Removing or weakening focus indicators makes keyboard/assistive navigation inaccessible; hover/focus states exist to make the control easier to perceive, and default outlines can be nearly invisible on dark backgrounds. Using `:focus-visible` shows focus indicators for keyboard/assistive focus while avoiding persistent focus outlines after mouse clicks, preserving accessibility and improving UX.
common_pattern: Accessibility-focused styling rules for interactive elements' focus/hover states: ensuring focus indicators remain visible, are not removed without replacement, and use the correct pseudo-class.

text: Forced-colors / high-contrast accessibility styles must be scoped inside `@media (forced-colors: active)` using CSS system color keywords (e.g., `CanvasText`, `Canvas`, `ButtonText`) rather than hard-coded color values or project `$color--*` variables; keep non-contrast-specific visual affordances (e.g., increased `stroke-width`) outside the query so the default design is unchanged.
reason: System color keywords adapt to the user's forced-color palette, whereas hard-coded colors (even white) may be invisible or low-contrast. Unconditional forced-colors overrides leak into normal rendering and unexpectedly change default layouts/colors, so they must be media-query scoped.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern CSS/Sass accessibility: ensuring color contrast for text/graphics across default, variant/state, and forced-colors (WHCM) rendering modes, including correct use of forced-colors media queries and system color keywords.

text: Do not rely on `background-color` alone to convey a component's boundary or grouping; add a border, outline, or other non-color visual affordance so the component stays legible in WHCM / forced-colors mode.
reason: Forced-colors mode overrides author background colors, so background-only treatments lose their visible structure and contrast, making the UI hard to read.
common_pattern: All generalizations concern CSS/Sass accessibility: ensuring color contrast for text/graphics across default, variant/state, and forced-colors (WHCM) rendering modes, including correct use of forced-colors media queries and system color keywords.

text:
When rendering Wagtail RichText field values in templates, always pass them through the `|richtext` filter, wrap the output in a block-level element such as `
` (never `

`, since richtext emits block-level HTML), and chain `|striptags` after `|richtext` when the target UI element requires plain text (e.g. a card description).
reason:
Without `|richtext` the raw field value (HTML source) is emitted instead of rendered content; a `

` wrapper around block-level richtext output produces empty or invalid nested paragraphs; `|striptags` keeps markup out of plain-text UI.
common_pattern: Wagtail rich-text handling: how RichText fields should be configured (restrictive feature allowlists, RichText vs CharBlock choice) and how their values should be rendered in templates (|richtext filter, block-level <div> wrapper, |striptags for plain text).

text: In HTMX templates, each element should declare each htmx attribute (e.g. `hx-swap`) at most once. Include the necessary hx-method attribute (e.g. `hx-get`) to trigger requests; an `href` alone is not sufficient. However, when an ancestor has `hx-boost="true"`, omit redundant `hx-get` on descendant links to avoid conflicting attributes.
reason: Duplicate htmx attributes are invalid and cause unpredictable swap behavior; missing hx-method attributes prevent the intended request; hx-boost already derives the request from `href`, making explicit `hx-get` redundant.
common_pattern: Adopt idiomatic HTMX patterns in Django templates instead of manual header checks, inline JavaScript, or ad-hoc attribute usage.

text: Reuse the project's shared Sass abstractions before writing raw CSS: check `abstracts/_mixins.scss` and `utilities/_utilities.scss` for an existing mixin, variable, or utility class that already implements the intent, and define new ones in those established partials rather than hard-coding values or redefining them in component files. Name new mixins for their general purpose (not component-specific prefixes) so they stay discoverable across components.
reason: The project maintains abstracts (mixins, variables) and utilities intended for reuse; reinventing values inline duplicates logic, adds magic values, and drifts from convention. General-purpose naming keeps abstractions discoverable for adoption across components.
common_pattern: Sass/SCSS organization in the wagtailio project: reuse centralized abstractions (mixins, variables, utilities defined in abstracts/ and utilities/ partials) instead of hard-coding or duplicating, and keep component-specific styles in their own component partial rather than in broader layout or global files.

text: Place styles at the correct Sass scope: component-specific styles (including print overrides) belong in a dedicated `_{component}.scss` partial under `components/`, not embedded in broader layout partials (e.g. `_header.scss`) or global files (e.g. `base/_print.scss`); reserve shared/global partials for generic rules. Only introduce a component partial when the component genuinely needs custom styling.
reason: Keeps component styles together for findability and consistency with the rest of the site, reduces CSS bloat and maintenance burden, and prevents global files (like `base/_print.scss`) from drifting out of sync with component styles over time.
common_pattern: Sass/SCSS organization in the wagtailio project: reuse centralized abstractions (mixins, variables, utilities defined in abstracts/ and utilities/ partials) instead of hard-coding or duplicating, and keep component-specific styles in their own component partial rather than in broader layout or global files.

text: Use the shared spacing mixins (e.g. `sf-spacing` from `wagtailio/static/sass/abstracts/_mixins.scss`) for component margins/padding instead of hardcoded pixel values, and reduce spacing values at mobile breakpoints (e.g. large breakpoint values dropping to ~20px on mobile). Keep a clear spacing hierarchy within a component: smaller margins between related elements (e.g. heading to content) and larger margins between distinct groups (component to next section), with a heading's `margin-bottom` never exceeding the component's bottom margin.
